  **Questions for the maintainer from the review**, each taken provisionally as written:

  5. *What a program's write drives.* The oven's eight zone lamps, `zone_hot bool[8] at
     card.q.0`, are written by one program through its `var_external`, `ote zone_hot[2]`
     only. As built that drives `zone_hot[2]` alone, so the configuration is warned that

     connection drives one element; a write through a tag subscript, `ote zone_hot[z]`,
     drives every lamp. Until the review any write through a var_external drove the array
     whole and nothing was warned. The options: (a) as built, by element; (b) any write
     drives the array whole, so the engineer is warned only of an array no program
     writes. Logix has no such check; decision 48's warnings are logex's own.
  6. *A coil and a latch on one lamp through one subscript.* `ote lamps[slot]` and `otl
     lamps[slot]` in one program: as built warned, "`lamps[slot]` is in `lamps`, which the

     it", as `ote w.[n]` beside `otl w.[n]` is (M5-9), where `ote lamps[2]` beside `otl
     lamps[2]`, and `ote b` beside `otl b`, are not. The operator sees lamp `slot` set by
     whichever rung comes last, as with `lamps[2]`. The options: (a) as built, since a
     write through a tag subscript is a write of the array whole (§4.12); (b) none where
     both name the same element through the same tag, as for a literal element, and the
     same for `w.[n]`. No such warning was found in IEC or the Logix extracts read
     (**unverified**).
  7. *A tag refused for its initial value.* `var r int 40000`: an int cannot hold 40000.

     initial value, so a rung `xic r ote lamp` is told what is wrong with that rung, an

     array refused for its initial list is (M5-11); (b) as before, the line declaring

- **M5-14 · Arrays of instances.** Decision 154: `var lane_t ton[4]`, `var lanes
  seal[4]`, a literal subscript on every instruction that runs one, a tag subscript on a
  member's read or write. *Done when* each refusal is pinned, the one-run rule holds per
  element (`ton lane_t[2] 500` twice refused), decision 85's two counter rungs hold per
  element, an edit of a lane's timer resumes it by its path `lane_t[2]`, a counter's edge
  memory on an element is on the block list by its path, an event task's timer, counter
  and one-shot warnings name each element, a `cal` of an element runs only its instance,
  and the contract walk draws arrays of instances. *Size L.*

  **Status: DONE — landed 2026-10-24**, as gated commits: `382777e` lands the item, code
  and tests; `9a84ed7` holds a configuration edit's accept for a program of no array of
  instances to its cost before the item and pins the mutants its table left alive; and a
  third holds the documents. The syntax was recorded first, in `3519c43`: a
  member after an element's subscripts, `lane_t[2].dn`, in the printer's generator and
  `@required_shapes` and 13 sources of the golden record, which the front end already read.
  The maintainer re-confirmed decision 154's literal rule on 2026-10-24. README's "Arrays of instances"
  is the run of `lanes.exs`, a sorter of four lanes, real output re-run on the item's code.

  An array of instances is the program's own: `var lane_t ton[4]`, `var lane_c
  ctu_int[4]` and `var gates gate[4]`. It is one to three dimensions of every timer, the
  long ones among them, every counter, the typed ones among them, or a user block, and its
  state is a tuple of instance maps in the elements' order (`Logex.FbType.started/2`).
  Each of the following is refused at its line, from Elixir too: an initial list; a
  var_input, var_output or var_external; an array of a block inside that block, at any
  depth; a configuration's global, `var_global w ton[2]`; and a connection. A host's input
  naming one is refused too.

  Each instruction that runs an instance takes an element by literal subscripts: a timer,
  a counter's side, a `cal`, and a one-shot's storage bit or a pulse coil's pulse bit (a
  bool element). The element is lowered with its name by value, so each rule holds per
  element:
  - M1-6's one-run rule, `ton lane_t[16#2] 30` beside `ton lane_t[2] 30` refused;
  - decision 85's preset agreement of a `ctud`'s two rungs;
  - each element's own preset;
  - nothing after an element's instruction on its path.

  An element a tag subscripts in such a slot is refused and told why: "`ton` runs
  `lane_t[i]`, whose subscript `i` holds: an instruction that runs an instance takes an
  element of an array of instances by literal subscripts, as in `ton lane_t[0]`, so that
  each element is one instance, run by one instruction whatever the program does". A
  `cal` of an array whole is told its element. A counter of one kind on the other's
  instruction is told its array's declaration, "declare its array `var lane_c ctud[4]`".

  A member of an element, `lane_t[slot].dn` or `lane_c[1].pv`, is read and written as an
  instance's member is, by literal or tag subscripts, and so are its bits. A subscript out
  of its dimension is M5-12's major fault, every subscript in `read`. A one-shot's storage
  bit in a member of an element is refused, as in a member of an instance. A `cal` of an
  element runs its body over that element's state alone. Its `:ran` record, its block
  list and a fault's `path` are by the element's name, `lanes[1]`.

  Every fact of an element is by its path: `lane_t[2]`, or `lanes[1].t` at depth. That
  holds in:
  - the walks;
  - the edit's plan, which resumes a timer and moves its preset, `{:preset, "lane_t[2]",
    {30, 50}}`, blocks a counter's edge memory, `lane_c[1].cu`, and a block's one-shot,
    `lanes[1].e`, and reports a member unwritten;
  - the event task's timer, counter and one-shot warnings;
  - `Logex.Runtime.get/2`, `m1.lane_t[2].acc`, which refuses an element or an array of
    instances named whole.

  An array of instances whose sizes or element type change is refused, as an array's is,
  and so is one whose user block's members change kind, by the first element's path. A
  state's array of instances is checked whole, a tuple of its sizes, each element its
  type's map, at depth in a block. The loader reads a block's name from a declaration with
  sizes, so `var gates gate[4]` loads `gate.ld`.

  *Done when*, each met:
  - Each refusal is pinned (`instance_array_test.exs`), `ton lane_t[i] 500` told why.
  - The one-run rule holds per element, however the subscript is spelled.
  - Decision 85's two counter rungs hold per element.
  - An edit resumes a lane's timer and moves its preset by its path `lane_t[2]`.
  - A counter's edge memory on an element is on the block list by its path until a scan
    runs it, and so is one on a rung a jump skips.
  - The event-task warnings name each element.
  - A `cal` of an element runs only its instance.
  - The contract walk draws arrays of instances:
    - a `ton` array of one or two dimensions, a `ctu` or `ctud` array and a gate block's;
    - members through a tag subscript, now and then out of range;
    - restarts, a misfit state refused, and edits that move a preset or block an edge;
    - a resource read through `get/2`;
    - against an oracle of each element as a scalar instance of its type, its reach every
      kind in `@ia_reach`.
  - `end_to_end_test.exs`, "arrays of instances in the plant (M5-14)", runs a sorter of four
    lanes from files on disk, `gates gate[4]` loaded from `gate.ld`, over 600 seeded cycles
    against an oracle that knows nothing of logex.

     value read. A host's `force/3` gives a value, not text, and is quoted as the value.
     The options: (a) as built, the text as written; (b) the value read, as decision
     226's example was pinned; (c) both, "got: 16#ffffffff, which is 4294967295". Logix
     keeps forces in the project, not a file (1756-PM004L pp.52–53), so offers no

  rounds: `real_trunc_int` given an lreal source was told "use `lreal_to_int`", given a
  dint destination "use `real_to_dint`", and given a real destination "use `move`", none
  of which truncates, where decision 148 tells a conversion's slot the conversion that
  does the whole job. It is now told `lreal_trunc_int` and `real_trunc_dint`, and a real
  destination nothing (provisional, question 1); a source of an integer or a bit string
  is still told its conversion. `real_test.exs` pins each, failing with the fix reverted;
  decision 162 notes it.

  **Questions for the maintainer** *(answered on 2026-10-26: 1 changed, a truncation into a
  real told it writes an integer, decision 260; 2 confirmed, as declared, decision 261;
  below, after M5-16's review)*.
  1. *A truncation into a real.* A programmer writes `real_trunc_int fan_hz shown`, the
     fan's 37.9 Hz to show as 37, but declared `shown` a `real`. The compiler refuses it;
     what does the message suggest? (a) Nothing, as built: "`real_trunc_int` writes an
     int, but `shown` is a real (declared on line 2)"; (b) "use `move`", as before, though
     a move would show 37.9; (c) say why, "no instruction truncates into a real: declare
     `shown` an integer type". IEC's TRUNC writes only an integer (Ed 3 Table 22 feature
     2b, decision 162); Logix's TRUNC writes a REAL or LREAL destination too
     (1756-RM018A-EN-P pp.828–829), so a Logix programmer may expect one.
  2. *An initial value reported as declared.* An edit gives `var_output speed real` an
     initial value, `1.0e-30`. The report reads `{:initial_changed, "speed", {0.0,
     1.0e-30}}`, the value as written, though a real holds it as 1.0000000031710769e-30,
     which a restart will start it at. (a) As declared, as built, decision 157's "compared
     exactly as declared", so `0` edited to `0.0` is reported though both start at 0.0;
     (b) the value it will start at, so the operator sees what a restart gives, and `0`
     to `0.0` reported no more; (c) both, `{0.0, 1.0e-30}` beside what it starts at. The
     walk found the two edits differ today: a configuration's `var_global speed real
     1.0e-30` is held at its nearest as the file is read, so a configuration edit reports
     `{0.0, 1.0000000031710769e-30}`, while `var_global x real 0` still reports `0`, as
     written; the walk restates each as built. Logix has no declared initial value but the
     value a download carries, unverified.

  **Questions for the maintainer** (M5-15's review) *(answered on 2026-10-26: 3 changed to
  (c), the 0 tried again at each poll and `status/1` naming each device not known to be 0,
  decision 262; 4 changed to (b), "it would be read as 0.0", decision 263; 5 changed to
  (b), every walk's and end-to-end test's oracle in clauses, decision 264; below, after
  M5-16's review)*.
  3. *A trip's 0 that a device does not take.* A conveyor's drive card is told to stop:
     the runner trips, on a bit number out of range say, and writes every output 0 once,
     but the card's write fails that moment (a cable glitch, `{:error, :eio}`). Today the
     runner passes the failure over, as decision 135's "where it still takes a write"
     has it: the card keeps showing its last outputs, the conveyor's run bit still 1, and
     nothing tries again until a restart. What should an operator see? (a) As built: one
     zero, and the card's own fault behaviour is relied on; (b) the zero tried again at
     each poll while the runner is tripped, until one is taken; (c) (b), and `status/1`
     names each device whose outputs are not known to be 0. IEC says nothing. In Logix the
     output module itself goes to its configured fault state when the controller faults
     or its connection is lost, "A major fault on the controller causes the outputs to go
     to their configured fault state" (1756-UM900B p.242) and "the output remains in the
     Fault mode state until a connection is re-established" (1756-UM058L p.83), so the
     module, not a write from the controller, holds the safe state.
  4. *Decision 250's words for a comparison.* `gt 1.0e-310 0.0` is refused "…: it would be
     written as 0.0", words decision 240 took from a write; a comparison writes nothing.
     (a) Keep them, one message for every slot; (b) "it would be read as 0.0" in a
     comparison's slots alone; (c) "the comparison would compare 0.0". IEC and Logix have
     no such message; unverified for Logix's handling of a denormal constant.
  5. *Clauses, not conditionals, in tests.* CLAUDE.md's rule is enforced on `lib/` by a
     grep; the test files hold some 300 `if`, `cond` and `case`, most in the walks' draws
     and harnesses. This review made the cross-type walk's oracle clauses. (a) `lib/` only,
     as now; (b) every walk's oracle too, the draws free; (c) all test code, with the grep
     extended. IEC and Logix have nothing to say here.

  *Provisional readings* (the answers'), each a question for the maintainer *(every one
  answered on 2026-10-27, decisions 286 to 289, below)*:
  1. *A stop while a device's 0 has not been taken.* The runner tripped, the drive card's 0
     failed, and the host stops the runner before the card's next poll. As built the close
     writes nothing more, as before decision 262, so the card keeps its last outputs. The
     options: (a) as built; (b) the close tries the 0 once more, as the poll would have.
     Logix leaves the safe state to the module's own fault behaviour (1756-UM900B p.242).
     The close's review puts this question first, as a safety point: a tripped runner
     whose card's 0 fails at every attempt, stopped, closes the card still showing 1, with
     no last attempt, which sits uneasily with decision 116's "every output 0 once" at a
     stop; it recommends (b). Not settled here: it is the maintainer's.
  2. *A device down at the trip.* A drive killed or gone down when the runner trips is named
     in `status/1`'s `unzeroed` until a restart, its outputs not known to be 0; one whose 0
     was taken and that goes down later is not named. The options: (a) as built; (b) a
     device that goes down while tripped named too, though its 0 was taken.
  3. *A member's whole write beside a bit of it through a tag subscript.* `move 5
     lane_c[1].pv` beside `ote lane_c[i].pv.3`, either first, is warned of nothing, where
     `move x c.pv` beside `ote c.pv.3` is the second-`ote` warning. The options: (a) as
     built; (b) warned, "`lane_c[i].pv.3` is in `lane_c`, as `lane_c[1].pv` is, which the
     `move` on line 12 writes whole".
  4. *A comparison beside a tag* (decision 263's reading). `eq l 1.0e-310`, `l` an lreal,
     is told "… which never holds it: … it would be read as 0.0", the comparison's own
     slot, where the question asked of two literals. The options: (a) as built; (b) "written
     as 0.0" beside a tag, the literal held in the tag's type.

    :cold`, writes the store before it releases or reads any device; a failed write leaves
    the runner tripped as it was, or not started, every output still 0. M6-5 builds it so.

    start using the last periodic or event write; confirmed, and README's "What logex is

**What stays deferred**, each a later item or milestone (§4.12): the TIME and LTIME types,
the dates and `T#` literals; strings and characters; enumerations, named values and
subranges; structures, UDTs and directly derived types; typed literals, `int#5`, and
octal; references; IEC's array bounds, `ARRAY[*]`, more than three dimensions and
whole-array `copy` and `fill`; IEC's byte and word partial access, `w.%B1`; online
widening; `round`, `ceil` and `floor`; the BOOL, BCD and real-to-bit-pattern conversions;
and nanoseconds in the core's clock. Not adopted: pointers, unions, target-width integers
and Logix's literal suffixes.

**Milestone 5 is done when** a program and a configuration of §4.4's plant, loaded from
files on disk, declare and run every type decision 144 and 155 name, the fan's speed a
`real` from the drive card and its eight zone temperatures a located `real[8]`, the box
counter a typed counter and its weights an array indexed by a tag, through `Logex.Runner`
on the manual clock against an oracle that knows nothing of logex; an integer result past
its width wraps with no power, a real's saturates, and no infinity, NaN or −0.0 ever
reaches a state; every mixed-type operand Figure 11 does not widen is refused naming its
conversion, and every conversion rounds as IEC's examples say; an index or a bit number
out of range trips the runner with every output 0 once, and a negative square root is a
minor fault, `:negative_sqrt`; an online edit of a type or a
size is refused, and a changed initial value of every type is reported; and the contract
walks reach every type, refusal and trip reason, repeating exactly.


### Milestone 6 — retained values and a true warm restart

**Designed and decided 2026-10-27** (`docs/organisation.md` §4.13 and §7, decisions
266–285; "decision N" in this section is that §7's). The maintainer asked for it after
Milestone 5 closed, from README's "What logex is not": today a warm restart is a cold one,
so a counter's count, a totaliser's total or a timer's accumulated time is lost when the
runner restarts, crashes or the VM stops. A design pass on `3a7c2eb` read IEC 61131-3 Ed 2
and Ed 3 in full, the conventional family's prescan rows, power-up handling and stored
images (1756-RM018A, RM094N, PM010N, PM014O, PM017J, UM001Q, UM543T, UM900B), Siemens'
retentive memory and starts, and CODESYS's and Beckhoff's RETAIN and PERSISTENT; its
review corrected seven facts and added two questions (284 and 285). The maintainer
answered all twenty on 2026-10-27, each as recommended:
- only what a program marks is retained, an unmarked tag initialised at a warm start, as
  logex's answer to IEC's implementer-specific rule (266);
- `var retain count dint` and `var non_retain count dint`, both words reserved, never on
  one line together (267), on a program's `var` and `var_output`, a block's three
  sections and `var_global`, and refused on a program's `var_input` and on `var_external`
  (268), of every elementary type, arrays and instances whole, hidden members included
  (269), the nearest mark on a member's path winning (270);
- a fresh start with a store warm unless `start: :cold`, and a cold restart writing the
  store before its first round (271); `retain` on a located global refused, a retained
  var_output driving an output point warned of, README naming the hazard (272);
- an outage not counted, a timer resuming (273), and `first: true` on every start, warm
  or cold, so no edge fires on the first scan (274), and no prescan (279);
- the store written every `retain_period:`, 1000 ms unless set, and at a trip, a stop and
  a cold restart, atomically, by a writer process of its own, a failed write reported and
  the plant running on (275), in readable text under a header (276), matched by
  instance, program type, path, exact type and fit, member by member, the rest dropped and
  reported in `status/1` and only a malformed file refused (277), and a store of another
  configuration refused, `start: :cold` starting over it (285);
- an online edit of a qualifier reported, `:retain_added` and `:retain_removed`, and
  nothing written (278);
- a pure core image and a runner-owned file (282); `persistent` and `program retain`
  deferred, `persistent` not reserved (280, 281), the scope as listed (283), and nothing
  special for a retained value that tripped the plant (284).

Decisions 38, 44, 69, 76, 113, 115, 116, 127, 133 and 188, and §5's RETAIN row, carry

Each item lands as Milestone 5's did: its words surveyed in `docs/naming.md` first,

and configurations it breaks; a gated series, each commit gated alone by `mix format

code, every survivor given a test. Throughout:

- **The core stays pure** (decision 282): no clock and no file in `Logex.Runtime`; the

Sizes use Milestone 5's key: **S** under about 30 lines of `lib/` and its tests, **M** 30
to 150, **L** 150 to 500, **XL** more, or a spike first. The record's estimate for the

with tests two to four times that.

globals; the image; the store at events, then the periodic writer; the edits, whose

  *Provisional readings of M6-1 and M6-2*, each a question for the maintainer *(every one
  answered on 2026-10-27, decisions 293 to 298, below)*:
  1. *The first scan after a warm restart counts its own time.* Decision 273 sets a
     retained timer's `last` to its instance's `now`, its last scan's, so the time before the restart since
     the timer last ran is not counted, a frozen block's or a skipped rung's; but the first
     scan after it counts the time the host passes in it, as any scan does. The conveyor's
     lube `rto` stands at 62 hours when the runner trips; at a warm restart the runner
     moves its anchor, so the operator sees 62 hours and then only the motor's running
     after the restart. A host of the core alone that restarts and then scans with
     `elapsed_ms` of an hour sees the lube timer add that hour. The options: (a) as built,
     the host's `elapsed_ms` the time that passed; (b) a timer adds nothing on a first
     scan, which would change every timer clause's cost. M6-2's done-when says "without
     counting the gap between the restart and the next scan's `now`", read here as the
     time before the restart; `retain_test.exs` pins (a). Logix's RTO adds `current_time −
     last_time_scanned` (1756-RM018A p.112); whether its first scan after a power cycle
     counts the outage is unverified (§4.13).
  2. *A line refused for its qualifier alone still declares its tag*, with none, so its
     uses are checked and not each told it is undeclared: `var_external retain estop
     bool` is told once, as M5-13's review's scalar refused for its initial value alone is.
     On the conveyor, a program whose e-stop line is so refused gets one message, not one
     more for each of the ten rungs that read `estop`. Since M6-2's review this holds for
     every refusal of a qualifier alone, one out of place or given twice among them
     (reading 3). The options: (a) as built; (b)
     declare nothing, every use then told it is undeclared. Neither IEC nor the Logix
     manuals saved say how a compiler recovers from a bad declaration (none found).
  3. *A qualifier out of its place is told where it goes*: `var count retain dint` and
     `var count dint retain` are "`retain` comes straight after the section word, as in
     `var retain count dint`"; since M6-2's review such a line is read without it and
     declares its tag, with the qualifier in its place where it has one, as reading 2
     has it, and `var retain non_retain count dint` and `var retain retain count dint`
     declare theirs with none, neither word being taken. IEC writes the word after the
     section keyword only (Ed 3 Annex A, p.224), over a section; Logix has no qualifier
     (§4.13). A box counter declared `var boxes ctu retain` is refused, and its count is
     kept only once written `var retain boxes ctu`. The options: (a) as built; (b) taken in
     either place.
  4. *`Logex.Tag.new!/5`*: from Elixir the qualifier is a fifth argument, `new!("c",
     :dint, :var, nil, :retain)`, `new!/4` kept as it was, so no host's call changes. The
     options: (a) as built; (b) a keyword list. No standard speaks to it.
  5. *`Program.retained`'s paths*: a sorted list of strings, a path whole where everything
     under it is retained, `boxes`, and otherwise each retained member, `s1.k`, an array
     of block instances' members by `[*]`, `gates[*].k`, as decision 259's messages write
     a path into every element. M6-4's image and M6-5's store name each value by its own
     path, `m1.boxes.cv`; this list is the compile's settling, never the store's lines.
     The options: (a) as built; (b) every leaf listed, `boxes.cv`, `boxes.cu` and the rest,
     which a reader of `retained` would see in full at the cost of a longer list. No
     standard speaks to it.
  6. *A configuration file's `retain` until M6-3* (raised by M6-2's review). The
     configuration file reserves no `.ld` word today, so `var_global retain total bool`
     is read as a global named `retain` of an unknown type `total`, and `var_global
     retain bool` and `program non_retain m` are accepted, a global and an instance so
     named. Once M6-3 lands, `var_global retain bool` changes meaning or is refused. On
     the conveyor, an operator whose plant file names a global `retain` sees it start
     failing to load at M6-3. The options: (a) M6-3 reserves both words in a
     configuration file's names too, as `.ld` reserves them, such a plant file then
     refused with the word named; (b) M6-3 reads a qualifier only where a type follows
     it, `var_global retain bool` still a global named `retain`. IEC writes the
     qualifier after the section keyword over a section, `VAR_GLOBAL RETAIN` (Ed 3
     §6.5.6 and Annex A, p.224), and reserves its keywords everywhere; Logix has no
     qualifier (§4.13). Left to M6-3, its entry says so.

     different: an output point starts at 0 and an input point is read at every start
     either way. The options: (a) as built, the word stating the default; (b) refused as
     `retain` is, a located global taking no qualifier. IEC qualifies `VAR_GLOBAL` over a
     section, `NON_RETAIN` there in §6.5.6.2's text but not the grammar (Ed 3, pp.57 and
     224), and retains located variables (p.58); Logix has no qualifier (§4.13).

  7. *A retained global that is a task's `single`* (M6-3's review). With `var_global
     retain arm bool` and `task ev single arm priority 0`, a warm restart keeps `arm` at 1.
     The trigger's last sample goes back to 0, as after every restart (M2-6), so the first
     cycle runs `ev` though `arm` never rose. Decision 274 keeps a program's edges from
     firing on the first scan, but a `single` is not one of the program's edges. What the
     operator sees: (a) as built, the event task runs once just after the warm restart,
     as it would for an input point that is already 1 (decision 51); (b) the trigger's
     last sample taken from the kept value, so `ev` waits for the next real rise; (c) a
     retained `single` refused or warned of. IEC's SINGLE is a rising-edge trigger and
     says nothing about restarts; Logix has no qualifier (§4.13), and how its event tasks
     meet a power-up is not in the record's extracts (**unverified**).
  8. *A retained global a connection drives* (M6-3's review). With `var_global retain
     total dint 0` and `w1.count total`, where `count` is not retained, `total` is 2 before
     a warm restart and still 2 just after it. `w1`'s first run then copies its `count`,
     back at 0, over it, so the operator sees the kept total come back for one round and
     then drop to 0, with no warning. With `var_output retain count dint` it stays 2. What
     the operator sees: (a) as built, no warning; (b) a warning, as decision 272 gives for
     output points: "`total` is retained but driven by `w1.count`, which is not: the first
     round writes over it"; (c) refused. IEC and Siemens leave this to the programmer, and
     Logix has no qualifier.

  and every retained timer starts at the start's `now` (decision 188 holding); and the
  take-out's cost is bounded in the retained count. *Size L.*

  a lone instance's image, `%{program: name, kinds: kinds, values: values}`, each retained

  `retained/1` a resource's, `%{configuration: name, globals: globals, instances:
  instances}`, each retained global and each instance whose program retains anything,
  none set aside, the program running during an edit; `instance/2` and `start/2` start a
  new instance or resource and lay the image over it by decision 277's matching, giving
  `{state, dropped}` and `{runtime, dropped}`. Each stored kind is judged before what is
  under it, and each value after its kinds: declared, of exactly its type or kind, an
  array of the stored sizes, retained by the changed program, and, a value, fitting it as
  a state's value does (decisions 171 to 188, `Logex.Image.fits?/2`); the first that
  fails is its reason, `:undeclared`, `{:retyped, stored, now}`, `{:resized, from, to}`,
  `:unretained` or `:misfit`, reported once, in path order, nothing under a dropped kind
  reported, an instance of another program type `{"m1", {:retyped, "motor", "pump"}}`; a
  user block's instance member by member and an array of instances element by element;
  a changed initial value keeping the stored one; a path newly retained starting at its
  own, unreported. Each retained timer starts with `last` at the start's `now`, 0, so the
  state check's decision 188 holds; `first` is true; and a `single` the image put back
  starts its trigger's last sample at that value, as decision 305 has a warm `restart/2`,
  so the resource cycles as the warm-restarted original does. An image no host could take
  from logex is one `ArgumentError`, a line each, pinned: no map of its parts, a path no
  logic names, an element entry (an array is retained whole), a kind or a type of no
  shape, an entry under an instance whose kind it does not hold or by an element outside
  its array, a path both a kind and a value, a timer's `last`, and an image of another
  configuration or program, a line naming both; a take-out over retained paths edited by
  hand a pinned line, decision 194's pattern. The rule beside `initial_env/1` is stated
  in `Logex.Program`'s doc and a global's in `Configuration.initial/1`'s, and the one-rule
  section of `Logex.Runtime`'s moduledoc gains `start/2`'s rows. `Logex.Runtime`'s public
  surface, which `runtime_test.exs` pins, gains `retained/1`, `retained/2`, `instance/2`
  and `start/2`, named in the pin's comment.

  Every clause of the done-when has its test in `retain_image_test.exs`: a resource of
  three tasks, an event task on a retained `single`, a retained global shared through
  `var_external`, a counter, an `rto`, an array, an array of timers, a block and a real
  started from another's image twelve times over seeded cycles, each next 25 cycles'
  outputs, events (their times the restart's `now` earlier), globals and images exactly
  those of the original after a warm restart; every mismatch the entry names, each
  dropped or kept with its reason, from source, a lone instance's and a resource's;
  misfits of every kind, a dint past its range, a bool of 2, a `real` no single holds, an
  integer in an `lreal`, −0.0, a list of the wrong length and an element outside its type;
  no timer's `last` in an image at any depth, each starting at 0 and scanning; and the
  growth. The contract walk (`api_contract_test.exs`) round-trips an image through a
  changed program: 60 seeded programs of six tags of drawn kinds and qualifiers and a
  block whose own members' are drawn, scanned, their image taken, now and then a value
  made a misfit, laid by `instance/2` over a changed program drawn from each (a tag
  renamed, removed, retyped, resized or requalified, the block's members retyped, added,
  removed or requalified), the state and the dropped list against decision 277 restated
  from the two specs alone, an unchanged program's start scanning as its warm restart
  does, and a host mistake at each of the four doors, its reach eleven `iw_` atoms, its
  draws in `@draws` and its oracle in clauses.

  *Cost.* Nothing that ran before changes: against `6b32b51`, a plant of 1 to 16
  motors compiles, checks, starts, cycles and restarts warm and cold in exactly the
  reductions it did, and a lone motor makes its instance, scans and restarts in exactly
  them (`instance` 453, `scan` 547, `warm` 476); at 64 motors every figure is within the
  run's noise, under 0.25%. The take-out is bounded in the retained count: a resource
  that also holds an unretained `int[16384]` takes out its 20 retained dints in exactly
  the reductions of one holding an `int[16]`, 585, and 160 retained dints cost under 4.4
  times 40. The matching grows linearly in the image, an array of 2048 retained timers
  under 4.6 times 512, the tuple built once a row. A configuration that retains nothing
  starts from its empty image within 120 reductions of `start/1` (145 for one motor, 1426
  for 64, about 22 an instance), and its take-out costs about 12 an instance.

  the reading nearest the record, IEC and Logix, each marked so in the code and in §4.13:

  1. *The image's shape*: a lone instance's `%{program:, kinds:, values:}`, its paths
     inside the instance, a resource's `%{configuration:, globals:, instances:}`, an

     whose members are the same, is told by its kind. An operator sees nothing of it until

     path as decision 276's store lines are, `%{"m1.boxes" => {:instance, "ctu"},
     "m1.boxes.cv" => {:dint, 41}}`, one map for a whole resource. *(Answered (a), decision 307.)*

     options: (a) as built, the stored preset kept; (b) the preset follows the program

     dropped list or a list of its own. *(Answered (b), decision 308: the preset follows the program, a stored one that differs reported in the dropped list.)*

     line naming both, decision 285's rule for a store carried into the core, so a

     built; (b) everything dropped and reported, `{"", :undeclared}`, the start going on. *(Answered (a), decision 309.)*

  - *A built-in's preset* (308): changed. At a start from an image a timer's `.pre` and a
    counter's `.pv` are the program's, the number on the instruction that runs the
    instance, as an edit's switch moves it; `.acc` or `.cv`, the done bits and the edge

    `dropped`, every entry being a stored value the start did not keep, and a misfit
    preset is `:misfit` as before (`Logex.Image`'s `fitted/4`, looked at only where a
    value's last segment is a built-in's preset member, `@preset_members`).
  - *An image of another configuration or program* (309): confirmed, refused.
  - *The drops in an array of instances* (310): changed. Where every element drops the
    same member for the same reason, once, `gates[*].j`, decision 259's path form, at any
    depth, `hs[*].ws[*].x`, the innermost arrays first, a resource's after its instance's
    name; where the elements differ, each by its element. `[*]` comes before any element
    in path order (`collapsed/2`, `ordered/1`).

    `lreal`, a tag's, a member's, an array's element or a global's, is taken at its

  *Provisional readings of the answers, put to the maintainer.* Where the answers are
  silent the work took the reading nearest the record, IEC and Logix, each marked so in
  the code and in §7:

  1. *A preset logic wrote* (decision 308). With `xic setup move 5000 t1.pre`, an operator's
     recipe changing the preset at run time, a warm restart after a trip keeps 5000, the
     instance kept as it was (decision 271), but a fresh start from the store gives the
     program's number again and reports `{"m1.t1.pre", {:preset, 5000, 3000}}`, so the
     operator sees the recipe's preset survive a trip and not a power cycle. The options:
     (a) as built; (b) a warm restart puts the program's preset back too, so both starts
     agree and the recipe is lost at either; (c) a preset logic writes is kept at a start
     from the store as well, the program's number only where no logic writes `.pre`.
     *Answered: (a), confirmed (decision 318, 2026-10-30).*
  2. *A `single` put back with no sample* (decision 313). An image of the host's own, or
     a configuration whose retained `arm` became a task's `single` since its image was
     taken, puts `arm` back at 1 with no sample: as built its event task does not run in
     the first cycle, the value standing for the sample (decision 305's rule). The
     options: (a) as built, nothing fires; (b) a sample of 0, as `start/1` has it, so the
     event task runs once in the first cycle; (c) refused, an image whose retained `single`
     has no sample being the host's mistake. *Answered: (a), confirmed (decision 319,
     2026-10-30).*
  3. *How a drop names an element written with leading zeros* (decision 312). A store
     edited by hand to `tl[01].acc 5000000000`, a misfit, is reported as `tl[1].acc`, the
     path logic names, not as the person wrote it. The options: (a) as built, by value;
     (b) as written in the store, so the person finds the line they typed. *Answered:
     (a), confirmed (decision 320, 2026-10-30).*

- **M6-5 · The store, read and written at events.** `Logex.Retain`, internal, its
  `encode/1` and `decode!/2` and the atomic write and read, the forces file's write rule

  synchronous as the forces file's are; `status/1`'s `retain` and the store's age
  (decisions 271, 275 and 285). `stop/2` made a call, since `GenServer.stop/3`, which it is
  today, ignores `terminate/2`'s return and always gives `:ok` (§4.13): the stop taken when
  the runner reaches it, never held for a slot, each waiting request answered as today,
  every output 0 once and every device closed (decision 116) before the store's write, so
  that no store write keeps an output on, then the reply, `:ok` or `{:error, {:retain,
  reason}}`, then the stop with its reason; with no `retain:`, `:ok` as today. Decisions 115's last sentence, 116, 127 and 133
  annotated as landed. *Done when*, on the manual clock: a runner stopped, or tripped and
  killed, and started fresh restores what its last write held, never older and never
  half; a cold restart's store write precedes its first round, and its release and read
  of every device (decision 291), and a crash right after it
  brings back none of the discarded values; a store that does not read is refused a line
  each, and one of another configuration is refused naming both; `start: :cold` ignores
  it and writes a new one at once; a cold restart whose store write fails leaves the
  runner tripped as it was, `{:error, {:retain, reason}}`, the store as it was, every
  output still 0 and no device released or read, and a fresh start with `start: :cold`
  whose write fails is not started, the same reason given, no device opened, the forces

  stops, every output 0 and every device closed first, and returns `{:error, {:retain,

  **Status: landed, 2026-10-30.** As the entry says, but where the readings below say
  otherwise. `lib/logex/retain.ex`, `Logex.Retain`, internal: `encode/2`, a resource's
  image as decision 276's text at a UTC time to the second, `logex retain 1`,
  `configuration <name> written <time>`, `global`, `trigger` (decision 313), `instance`,
  and each instance's kind and value lines in path order (`Logex.Image.ordered/1`, `t[2]`
  before `t[10]`), an array's elements on one line, a real in `Logex.Real.spelled/2`'s
  text, never a `last`; `decode!/2`, `{image, written_at}`, any number the lexer reads, a
  real at its type's nearest value, a subscript by its value as `Logex.Runtime.start/2`
  matches it (decision 312) and a stored preset reported as decision 308 has it, every
  line it cannot read a line of one `ArgumentError`, `<path>: line <n>: …`, in line
  order: a header of no store or of another version, no configuration line, a time that is
  none, another configuration (naming both and `start: :cold`, decision 285), a line of no
  shape, its words not one space apart among it, an unknown type or kind, a wrong count of
  values, a value no number, a line before any `instance` or not under its instance, a
  name that is none, and a second line naming one thing; `written/2`, the forces file's
  write rule, which `Logex.Runner`'s forces file now calls rather than its own copy; and
  `number/1`, the forces file's reading of a number, shared the same way. What a store's
  image holds is judged by `Logex.Runtime.start/2`, each of its lines naming the store.
  `Logex.Runner.Clock` gains an optional `wall_ms/1`, the monotonic clock's
  `System.os_time/1` and the manual clock's its own time from the epoch.

  The runner takes `retain:` and `start:`, checked in the caller after `forces:`, each in
  both pinned messages of `start_link/1`'s options: a path, none unless set; `:warm` or
  `:cold`, `:warm` unless set. A fresh start reads the store in the caller after the
  forces file and lays it over the resource by `Logex.Runtime.start/2`, a file that does
  not exist none; with `start: :cold` or no store file it writes the store at once, in the
  caller, before any device is opened, a write that fails giving `{:error, {:retain,
  reason}}` and starting nothing. A trip writes the resource as it left it, after every
  output is 0; a cold `restart/2` writes the resource as it restarts it, after the forces
  file is read and before any device is released or read, a write that fails answering
  `{:error, {:retain, reason}}`, the runner tripped as it was; `stop/2` writes after every
  output is 0 and every device closed, and answers `:ok` or `{:error, {:retain,
  reason}}`, stopped all the same; a warm restart, a crash, a kill and any other
  termination write none. Every write is synchronous, as the forces file's is, a failed one
  `{:retain, {:error, reason}}` to subscribers, a default kind, and `failed` in
  `status/1`'s `retain`, `%{path, written_at, failed, dropped}`, nil without `retain:`.
  `runtime_test.exs`'s surface pin gains `Logex.Retain`, hidden, and the clock's optional
  callback; `runner_test.exs`'s option and kind messages and `status/1` at start gain the
  new words and `retain: nil`.

  Every clause of the done-when has its test in `retain_store_test.exs`, on the manual
  clock: a runner stopped, or tripped and killed, and started fresh restores its last
  write, never an older one, and a write cut short leaves the store whole; a cold
  restart's write is seen by the device's own read before it, so it precedes the release
  and read, and a crash right after it restores none of what it discarded; a store that
  does not read is refused a line each, one of another configuration naming both; `start:
  :cold` ignores it and writes a new one at once; a cold restart whose write fails leaves
  the runner tripped as it was, the store as it was, every output still 0 and no device
  read or written; a fresh start whose write fails is not started, the reason given, no
  device read or written; a `stop/2` whose write fails stops, every output 0 and the
  device closed, and answers `{:error, {:retain, :eisdir}}`, its zeros seen by the
  device's last write before the store changed, and every existing pin of its `:ok`
  passes; a retained output-driving bit is written only by the first round; decision
  284's retained subscript trips the plant again at a warm fresh start and not at a cold
  one. Besides: a crash inside the runner (its `terminate/2` run) writing nothing, a warm
  restart writing nothing, the write synced before its rename (traced), a runner with no
  store taking no image out (traced), and the store's text linear in its lines. The
  end-to-end Done-when is `end_to_end_test.exs`'s "the store in the plant (M6-5)": §4.4's
  plant from files on disk with a retained box counter, `rto` and total through the runner
  with a store, 400 seeded steps of eyes, kills, stops and trips each followed by a fresh
  start, against an oracle that knows nothing of logex. The runner walk
  (`api_contract_test.exs`) gives its runner a store wherever it gives it a forces file,
  no draw added, its configurations a program, `keep`, whose retained count and a
  retained global it adds to the store keeps; its model restates each write, the first
  start's, a trip's and a cold restart's before its release, lays the last over a fresh
  start after a crash and checks the store's lines, its reach `:store_restored` and

  *Provisional readings, put to the maintainer.* Where the record is silent the item took
  the reading nearest the record, IEC and Logix, each marked so in the code and in §7's
  notes:

  1. *`stop/2` is a call in effect, not in form* (decisions 116 and 275). The record makes
     `stop/2` a call; a call waits on a runner suspended with `:sys.suspend/1` for ever,
     where `GenServer.stop/3`, a system message, stops it, which `runner_test.exs` pins.
     As built the caller names itself to the runner, stops it by `GenServer.stop/3`, and
     the runner answers it as it terminates, after its zeros, its closes and its write: an
     operator's stop returns `:ok` or `{:error, {:retain, reason}}` either way. The
     options: (a) as built; (b) a true call, a suspended runner's stop then waiting until
     it is resumed, and the pin changed. *Answered: (a), confirmed (decision 321).*
  2. *A clock without a wall clock* (decision 276). The header's time comes through the
     clock's `wall_ms/1`, an optional callback; a host's own clock without it runs a
     runner given no store, and one given `retain:` is refused at start, "the runner's
     clock `MyClock` has no wall_ms/1, which a runner given retain: writes its store's time
     by". The options: (a) as built; (b) the machine's wall clock, `System.os_time/1`,
     whatever the clock, so a test's store names the real time; (c) `wall_ms/1` required
     of every clock, a host's clock without it refused even with no store.
     *Answered: (a), confirmed (decision 322).*
  3. *`start:` with no store.* `start: :cold` or `start: :warm` given without `retain:` is
     refused, "the runner keeps no store, so start: :cold has none to start from: start it
     with retain: a path", as a force without `forces:` is. The options: (a) as built; (b)
     taken and passed over, so a host may always say `start: :cold`. *Answered: (a),
     confirmed (decision 323).*
  4. *A termination that is not `stop/2`.* A runner whose parent shuts it down, a
     supervisor's orderly shutdown among them, or whose clock goes down, writes no store,
     as one that crashes (decision 292): the operator whose host application is shut down
     by its supervisor gets back, at the next start, what the last trip, stop or cold
     restart wrote, and from M6-6 the last period's. The options: (a) as built, only
     `stop/2` writes; (b) a parent's shutdown writes as `stop/2` does, after the zeros.
     *(M6-5's review: the runner traps exits, so a supervisor's `:shutdown`, which
     `systemctl stop` or `Application.stop/1` gives, runs its `terminate/2`, which zeroes
     and closes and writes nothing: a box counter at 10,000 after a shift comes back at
     its start-of-shift value until M6-6, and at the last period's after it. The review
     recommends (b). Pinned as built by "a parent's shutdown writes nothing
     (provisional)", which (b) would turn round.)* *Answered: (b), changed (decision
     316): a parent's `:shutdown` or `{:shutdown, term}` writes as `stop/2` does, the
     clock gone and a crash still none.*
  5. *A cold restart a device refuses* (decision 291). The write comes before the release
     and the reads, so a cold restart refused by a card still bad has written the store
     with the initial values while the resource in memory keeps the old ones: a warm
     restart next keeps the old values, and a crash before it brings back the initial
     ones. The options: (a) as built, the cold restart asked for being taken as the
     discard; (b) the old store written back where the restart is refused. *Answered: (b),
     changed (decision 317).*
  6. *The first round's `{:retain, …}` event* (§4.13). No subscriber can exist before
     `start_link/1` returns, so the event a fresh start owes with the store's age and the
     drops reaches no one; `status/1`'s `retain` carries both. The options: (a) as built;
     (b) the event held and sent to the first subscriber. *Answered: (a), confirmed
     (decision 324).*
  7. *`retain:` naming the forces file* is refused, "the runner's retain: and forces: name
     one file", where the two writes would overwrite each other. The options: (a) as
     built; (b) taken. *(Since M6-5's review the refusal holds however the paths are
     spelled, `./x` and `x` one file, and refuses either naming the `.tmp` the other is
     written through, `retain: "x.tmp"` beside `forces: "x"`, which made every force write
     replace the store with the forces file's text.)* *Answered: (a), confirmed
     (decision 325).*

  *M6-5's review* (2026-10-30, `scratchpad/m6/r5`) found two high, two medium and five
  low findings; each is answered so, a test of its own failing where the answer is
  reverted:

  1. *The runner walk failed at 17 of 30 fresh seed families* (high): its model read the
     store after `start_link/1` returned, and a fresh start's first round that trips,
     forces from the forces file making a major fault, had written it again by then. The
     runner was right. The model now reads the store before the start (`store_text/1`),
     the first round's trip writing it as any trip does; an atom,
     `:store_tripped_at_start`, holds the walk to such a start, which the family
     `{2026, 10, n}` never reached, so the seed moved to `{4101, 10, n}`, where every atom
     is reached and the model read the old way fails. Of `{4101..4130, 10, n}` every walk
     passes (`scratchpad/m6/r6seeds.out`), eleven reaching every atom, the rest missing
     `:store_tripped_at_start` or one of `:zero_at_stop`, `:array_unforced` and
     `:next_due_from_step`, rare by their nature.
  2. *A hand-edited store crashed the start* (high): a type word with sizes went to
     `Logex.Declarations.array_word/1`, which trusts the lexer, so `real[3a]`, `int[2#]`
     and `real[]]` raised a `FunctionClauseError`, and `int[0]` and `int[-1]` were told
     how many values they hold. A type word and a kind with sizes are now read by the
     store's own rule (`sized_word/1`): one `[`, one to three sizes, each a whole number
     above 0 that `number/1` reads, 65,536 elements at most, and the `]` that ends the
     word, so `ton[3a` and `ton[4[`, which read as `ton[3]` and `ton[4]`, are refused
     too; each a line of the refusal, decoded and at a runner's start.
  3. *The trip's write order was not pinned* (medium): a test now trips the runner by a
     major fault, so the device's 0 is the runner's and not its own latch's, and sees the
     0 meet the store as the start wrote it, the trip's write after.
  4. *Provisional reading 4 loses a shift on an orderly shutdown* (medium): left
     provisional, as a question for the maintainer (reading 4 above), and pinned as built.
  5. *Survivors R7 and R2* (low): a header's time at `+05:00` or `-01:00` is refused,
     `Z` and `+00:00` taken; and `m1. dint 1` and `m1. ton`, which name nothing inside
     their instance, are refused.
  6. *`retain:` beside `forces:` by string equality* (low): the two are now compared by
     `Path.expand/1`, and neither may be the other's `.tmp`, three pinned lines (reading 7
     above).
  7. *The cold restart's cost* (low): "within noise" was loose. Measured again, three runs
     each, a runner with no `retain:` restarts cold at 64 instances in 49,248 to 49,313
     reductions against 49,247 to 49,249 at `aaae2bb` (up to +0.13%), and at 16 in 13,013
     to 13,098 against 13,090 to 13,539, a trip in 423 to 504 against 421 to 437
     (`scratchpad/m6/cost_base2.txt` and `cost_now2.txt`); the counts move between runs of
     one build here, and the review measured +2.7% and −3% on its own, so the change is a
     few percent either way, likely the runner's state map's layout, two keys more, and
     no clause a restart pays for.
  8. *The decision 300 test flaked* (low), at the base too: the reduction count of one
     configuration's check moves by up to 3 between two measures in one run, where the
     test held `drive` and `xrive` equal; the least of three moved too. It now holds them
     within 16 over the 64 located globals, a quarter of a reduction a global, where the
     lookup it guards against costs about 1,088 (a mutant that looks every device up
     fails by that); 60 runs alone, none failing, where 2 in 30 had.
  9. *README's "a fresh start" was inexact* (low): "What logex is not" now says a fresh
     start writes with `start: :cold` or no store file, never warm from a store, and that
     a supervisor's shutdown loses what changed since the last write, as built.

  *The answers to M6-5's readings* (the maintainer, 2026-10-30, `docs/organisation.md` §7
  decisions 316 to 325, built at `cdc3535`). Of M6-5's seven readings and M6-4's

  - *A parent's orderly shutdown* (316, reading 4): changed. A `:shutdown` or a
    `{:shutdown, term}` from the runner's parent, a supervisor's among them, which
    `terminate/2` sees as the runner traps exits, writes the store as `stop/2` does,
    after every output is 0 and every device closed, a failed write reported to the
    subscribers. A crash, a kill and the clock going down still write none (decision
    292). The clock's stop and the parent's take one path, `terminate/2`, the clock's
    told by its reason, `{:shutdown, {:clock, reason}}`, the runner's own exit, so it
    writes nothing as the record had it; a shutdown's write that meets the clock gone
    names no time and is none too. `retain_store_test.exs`'s "a parent's shutdown writes
    nothing (provisional)" is replaced by one pinning the write, its zeros first and the
    next fresh start restoring it; beside it a `{:shutdown, term}` and a supervisor's
    `Supervisor.stop/1`, a failed write reported, and a clock whose `now_ms/1` goes down
    while its wall clock answers writing nothing.
  - *A cold restart a device refuses* (317, reading 5): changed. The store is written back,
    after the refusal's zeros, with the values the runner still holds, the trip's, so a
    refused restart changes nothing on disk or in memory; a write-back that fails is
    reported as any failed write, `failed` and `{:retain, {:error, reason}}`, the runner
    tripped either way and the restart answered with the device's reason. A refused warm
    restart writes nothing. The runner walk's model restates it, its reach
    `:cold_written_back`.
  - Confirmed, as built: a preset logic wrote kept warm and the program's at a start from
    the store (318); a `single` put back with no sample starting at its value (319); a
    drop by the subscript's value, `tl[1].acc` (320); `stop/2` a call in effect only

    one, `status/1` carrying it (324); and `retain:` and `forces:` naming one file or

  *Provisional reading, put to the maintainer.* *A parent that ends `:normal`*
  (decision 316). The answer names `:shutdown` and `{:shutdown, term}`; a parent process
  that ends normally, which a supervisor never does but a host's own process that started
  the runner may, ends the runner `:normal`, and as built it zeroes and closes and writes
  no store, so a box counter at 10,000 comes back at the last trip's, stop's or cold
  restart's count. The options: (a) as built, only the two reasons the answer names; (b)
  `:normal` from the parent writes too, every orderly reason OTP has writing alike.

  changed (decision 328, 2026-10-30): every orderly exit writes; the test now pins the

- **M6-6 · The periodic writer.** `retain_period:`, its range settled (the record
  suggests 100 to 3,600,000 ms), the writer process, latest wins, the failed write's
  event `{:retain, {:error, reason}}` and status (decision 275). *Done when* a runner
  killed between two periods restores the earlier period's write; a write that fails
  leaves the old store, is reported, and the plant runs on; a `stop/2` while a period's
  write is in progress waits for it, drops any pending one and writes last, and one whose
  final write fails still stops and returns `{:error, {:retain, reason}}`; a slow write delays no
  round (the writer suspended with `:sys.suspend/1`); and a round with a store costs
  within a measured bound of one without, the take-out bounded in the retained count.
  *Size M.*

  **Status: landed, 2026-10-30.** As the entry says, but where the readings below say
  otherwise. `lib/logex/runner/writer.ex`, `Logex.Runner.Writer`, internal: a GenServer
  linked to its runner, started at the first period's write, handed one image at a time
  with its header's time, which it encodes and writes through `Logex.Retain.written/2`,
  `<path>.tmp` synced, closed and renamed over the store, and answers `{Logex.Runner.Writer,
  pid, at, result}`. The runner takes `retain_period:`, checked in the caller after
  `start:`, in both pinned messages of `start_link/1`'s options; its period's state is
  held under `retain`, so that a runner with no store holds exactly what it did. Every
  `retain_period:` ms, on a grid from its start on its clock, the runner takes the
  retained image out between rounds (`Logex.Runtime.retained/1`, through the hidden
  seam's `retained/1` where a test's module has one) and hands it to the writer, or, while
  a write is in progress, keeps it, the newest replacing the one that waited. A write made
  moves `status/1`'s `written_at`, the store's age; one that fails is `{:retain, {:error,
  reason}}` and `failed`, the store as it was and the plant running on. Every write at an
  event, a trip's, a stop's, a shutdown's and a cold restart's, first waits for the
  write in progress and drops the one pending, so that the event's is the last on disk.
  As the runner terminates, after the stop's or the shutdown's write, it stops the writer.

  Every clause of the done-when has its test in `retain_period_test.exs`, on the manual
  clock: a runner killed between two periods restores the earlier period's write; a write
  that fails leaves the old store, is reported, the plant running on, and the next
  period's clears `failed`; a stop while a period's write is in progress waits for it,
  drops the pending one and writes last, traced in the writer and the runner, and the
  writer is gone after; a stop whose final write fails stops and answers `{:error,
  {:retain, :eisdir}}`; a slow write, the writer suspended, delays no round, thirty rounds
  run on their times while three periods come, the one between dropped and the newest
  written; and a round with a store and a period of 3,600,000 ms costs within 10
  reductions of one with none, a period's take-out growing linearly in the retained
  values. Besides: `retain_period:`'s host mistakes, a pinned line each; 1000 ms unless
  set, `written_at` moving each second; the period's place among the rounds, told through

  passed inside a slow step taken once and the grid's next after it; a shutdown writing
  the resource as it was; a trip waiting for the write in progress and writing last;
  nothing written while tripped and a warm restart taking up the grid at its next due

  end-to-end test under CPU load pass (`scratchpad/m6/r50p.out`). `runner_test.exs`'s
  two option messages gain `retain_period:`; no other test line changed.

  *Mutations*, each judged by the full suite's exit code (`scratchpad/m6/m66mut2`): P1 the

  *Cost*, against `a6680c9`, the runner's reductions a round over 200 rounds of the fast
  task, the collector kept out by a large heap (`scratchpad/m6/m66cost`): with no store,
  1281.7 timed and 1226 untimed, exactly as before; with a store and a period of
  3,600,000 ms, 7 more a round, 1685.9 to 1692.9 for four retained counters, 0.4%; and at

  counters and 5,900 for 64. With the collector at work the counts move by a few either
  way, as the dummy key the parent was given showed.

  *Provisional readings, put to the maintainer.* Where the record is silent the item took
  the reading nearest the record, IEC and Logix, each marked so in the code:

  1. *The range and its defaults.* `retain_period:` takes a whole number of ms from 100 to
     3,600,000, the record's suggestion, 1000 unless set, nil as unset, as `forces:` and
     `retain:` take nil; given without `retain:` it is refused, "the runner keeps no store,
     so retain_period: 500 has none to write: start it with retain: a path", as `start:`
     is (decision 323). The options: (a) as built; (b) a wider range, 10 ms at the least,
     which an fsync every round of a fast plant comes near; (c) `retain_period:` without a
     store taken and passed over.
  2. *A grid from the start.* The periods are due at the start plus each whole period, as
     a periodic task's are; a due time passed while the runner was stuck in a step is
     taken once, just after it, and the next is the grid's next, none made up; a restart
     takes up the grid at its next due time, so that a warm restart writes nothing at
     once. Example: a period of 1000 ms, a runner stuck 2,500 ms in a step at 900 ms
     writes once at 3,400 ms and next at 4,000. The options: (a) as built; (b) every period
     counted from the last write, an event's among them, so that a cold restart at 1,700
     ms is next written at 2,700.
  3. *The take-out's place.* The take-out is the runner's own work between rounds: with
     untimed programs first in the share's slot that comes at or after its due time, out
     of its S ms, before the requests that waited, so up to C ms late, 4 ms at
     20%; with none at a wake of its own, or just after the round due with it, its
     outputs written, so the store holds that round. No round's due time moves for it.
     The options: (a) as built; (b) every take-out just after the round in progress at its
     due time, untimed or not, taking its time from the next round instead of from the
     slot.
  4. *Nothing written while tripped.* A tripped runner writes no period: the trip's write
     is the resource as the trip left it, and nothing a round changes until a restart. An
     edit stepped while tripped (decision 139) changes the resource, but its values reach
     the store only at the next event or period after a restart. Example: tripped, the
     operator tests an edit that adds a retained counter at 5; the host is then killed;
     the fresh start brings the counter back at its initial value. The options: (a) as
     built; (b) an edit's step while tripped writes the store, as a cold restart does.
  5. *An event write waits for the period's.* Every write at an event waits for the write
     in progress, in real time, for at most the idle watchdog and a poll period, as a
     device's close is bounded, and a writer still silent then is killed, its write
     reported `{:retain, {:error, :timeout}}`, the store the old or the new, the event's
     written after. Example: a disk that hangs for 2 s holds a stop for 510 ms with the
     defaults and then the stop writes, which may hang too. The options: (a) as built;
     (b) an unbounded wait, which the record's "waits for it" reads plainly, a hung disk
     then holding the stop for ever.
  6. *A writer gone down.* A writer that goes down, which no host can cause through the
     API, is reported `{:retain, {:error, {:down, reason}}}` where it held a write, and a
     new one makes the next period's write, the image waiting handed to it. The options:
     (a) as built; (b) the runner trips, `{:retain, ...}` among the trip reasons.
  7. *The store's age in `status/1`.* `retain`'s shape is unchanged: `written_at` moves
     with each write the writer makes, read when its answer comes, so between a take-out
     and its answer the status shows the write before. The options: (a) as built; (b)
     `status/1` gains the period and the time of the last take-out, `%{path, period,
     written_at, taken_at, failed, dropped}`.
  8. *Still open from M6-5's answers:* whether a parent's `:normal` exit writes the store,
     which decision 316 names neither way (pinned writing none, provisional). *Answered:
     changed, it writes (decision 328, 2026-10-30), with reading 11 below.*

  *Provisional readings, added by the review, put to the maintainer:*

  9. *How long a supervisor waits for a shutdown.* The runner's child spec gives
     `(devices + 2) * (idle + poll)` ms, never less than 5000: with the defaults a plant of
     up to eight devices keeps 5000 ms, and one of a device with `idle: 5000` 15,030 ms.

     ms.)* A shutdown longer than that is still killed and writes nothing. The options: (a) as
     built; (b) `shutdown: :infinity`, a hung disk then holding the supervisor's shutdown
     for ever; (c) every device closed at once rather than in device-name order (decision
     116), so the shutdown takes one close's time; (d) 5000 kept, the limit documented.
     *Answered: (a), confirmed, a host's own `shutdown:` winning (decision 326,
     2026-10-30).*
  10. *Who may shut the runner down with a write.* The runner tells a shutdown by its
     reason, `:shutdown` or `{:shutdown, term}`, not by who sent it, so
     `GenServer.stop(runner, :shutdown)` from any process writes the store as its
     parent's shutdown does, and its caller is answered `:ok` even where the write failed,
     the failure told only to the subscribers; `Logex.Runner.stop/2` answers it. The
     options: (a) as built; (b) only the parent's shutdown writes, any other process's
     `:shutdown` as a `:normal` stop. *Answered: (a), confirmed, `stop/2` remaining the
     call that returns the error (decision 327, 2026-10-30).*
  11. *Still open:* reading 8, whether a parent's `:normal` exit writes the store; the
     review leans to writing it, since the zeros and the closes come first. *Answered:
     changed, every orderly exit writes (decision 328, 2026-10-30).*

  **Status: landed, 2026-10-31** (`7713267`, the documents after it). As the entry says, but where the readings below say
  otherwise. `Logex.Edit.Plan` gives each plan `requalified`, built once at accept from
  the two programs alone: each program's leaves of state, a tag, an array of an elementary
  type and a built-in instance one leaf each, a user block's instance member by member at
  any depth and an array of them by `[*]`, each to whether the program retains it by
  decision 270's nearest mark as its `retained` settles it; a leaf both declare whose
  retention differs is in the change, one alone declares is not; and the change is named
  as `retained` names a path, a node whole where every leaf of either program under it
  changes alike, and otherwise each node below it that does. A switch, and so accept's
  forecast, reports each `{:retain_added, path, value}` or `{:retain_removed, path,
  value}`, read from the state after every other rule, and writes nothing; untest gives
  the reverse; no prune reports it. `Logex.Configuration.Edit` gives them by path through
  the plan's switch, by the instance's name, `t1.boxes`, beside a global's. Rows of
  `Logex.Edit`'s table and §4.9's; `@configuration_kinds` no longer holds the two kinds,
  which `@report_kinds` held since decision 302, so the lone edit's walk must reach them.

  *The rule stated* (the item asked it settled): a path is reported where its retention,
  by the nearest mark, differs between the two programs, compared leaf by leaf over what
  both declare, so `non_retain` and none are one (decision 302's reading); a mark moved
  between an instance and its members reports only the leaves whose retention it changes,
  `var retain s1 seal` to `var s1 seal` with `seal`'s `count` marked `retain` reporting
  `s1.run` and `s1.t` removed and nothing for `s1.count`, and a move that keeps the same
  leaves, `var retain l latch` to each of `latch`'s members marked, nothing. A qualifier
  changed with the type is refused for the type alone, as every type change is, so the
  edit reports nothing (§4.9). An array of a block's instances is reported once, by `[*]`,
  decision 310's and 259's form: a declaration marks every element alike, so no element
  can differ.

  PLAN's Done-when, each a test in `retain_edit_test.exs`: an edit that only changes a
  tag's qualifier reports it by path, the forecast equal to the test's report, and leaves

  retains it runs, after its test and after its assemble, and the lamp only while the
  original runs, at accept (before the test), after untest and after cancel; a warm
  restart after a trip keeps the count and loses the lamp under the candidate and the

  cancel and a second accept's test and assemble (the read at accept and the cancel's

  not yet caught up, so it finishes 30 ms late. The options, by what the operator sees:
  (a) a defect in the resume's rule ("the program that last scanned"), the timer to come
  back as it was, found and fixed with a test from this family; (b) the walk's round-trip
  rule too strict where an earlier edit superseded in the same configuration last
  scanned the instance, its oracle to allow the resume there; (c) left as it is until
  M6-8's contract walk. The record's reading is (a), since §4.9's resume rule says no
  resume is due between a test and an untest with no scan between, but it is not

  1. *M6-7's question 7613, traced.* At `{7613, 10, 19}` the instance `m2`, whose `rto`
     `t1` runs in an event task, is edited by a candidate that takes away the rung that
     runs `t1` (`xic in rto t1 30`) and moves `t1`'s `retain`; it is one edit, no other
     superseding it in between. Tested at 140 ms, the candidate scans `m2` once; untested
     at 140 ms, nothing resumes, no time having passed; the event task then does not run
     for 30 ms; tested again at 170 ms and untested at once, the untest resumes `t1` by 30
     ms, `{:resumed, "m2.t1", 30}`, since the program that last scanned `m2` is still the
     candidate. Those 30 ms were the original's, which ran `m2` from the first untest on
     but had no scan, so the timer would have caught them up at its next scan. So "an
     earlier edit's is unknown", option (b)'s reading, does not apply: it is the same
     edit. The operator sees a lube timer on a conveyor finish 30 ms late after a test and
     an untest made back to back. Options, by what the operator sees: (a) a defect in the
     resume's rule, which should ask who has held the instance since the last switch as
     well as who last scanned it, so the timer comes back as it was; (b) the rule right as
     written, the walk's round trip relaxed where the last scan was the stopped
     program's, and the 30 ms lost in this sequence documented; (c) left open. IEC
     61131-3 has no online edit; Logix's test and untest of edits run the original's
     timers as the original left them, and whether a Logix RTO not scanned catches up
     the time is not checked here (unverified). The record's reading stays (a), not
     built. *(Answered 2026-10-31: (a), decision 336, built below.)*

  *The maintainer's answers to M6-8's questions* (2026-10-31), recorded as decisions
  336–338 in `docs/organisation.md` §7 and built the same day:
  - *336, changed (a): the round trip's resume is a defect.* A timer resumed at an untest,
    or any switch back, comes back with exactly the time it had: the resume rule asks too
    who has held the instance since the last switch, so that time another program held,
    the original's from the first untest to the second test at `{7613, 10, 19}`, is never
    taken from it. *The rule, as built* (`Logex.Edit.Plan`, `Logex.Edit`'s moduledoc and
    §4.9's two rows): the edit's record of each instance keeps the time of its last
    switch, `held`; where no scan has run since that switch, the program it started, which
    this switch stops, has held the instance only since it, so a resume moves `last` on by
    `at - max(last, held)` (`at - held`, since `held` is then the instance's own `now`,
    which no `last` passes, decision 188), the time before it left for the timer to catch
    up; and a switch gives back what this edit's last switch moved of a timer's `last`, a
    resume or a resume given back, where no scan has run since and `last` is still where
    it left it, each move reported by its net, `:resumed` or `:resume_undone`, so that an
    untest after a test that gave an untest's resume back across a cycle with no scan
    gives that back in turn. Where a scan has run since the last switch, or this edit made
    none before, `last` becomes `now` as before: decision 56's pinned measurement (80 ms
    across a first switch) and an instance back from aside (decision 57) are unchanged,
    and fix F11's and decisions 93–95's resume tests stay green. *A lone instance* behaves
    as it did: its clock moves only by its own scans, so no program holds it unscanned for
    any time; 400 random sequences of scans, tests, untests, accepts and restarts of an
    `rto` on a rung a jump may skip gave every report and state the same at the parent and
    here (`scratchpad/m6/m9/x/lone_explore.exs`). *Tests*: `config_edit_test.exs`, the
    trace's conveyor, a lube `rto` in an event task tested, scanned, untested, held 30 ms
    by the original unscanned, tested and untested at once and done on time at its next
    run, and `m2`'s `t1` given back by an untest after a test that gave an untest's resume
    back, each failing with the change reverted; `edit_test.exs`, the lone conveyor,
    finishing on time, which passes at the parent too by the construction above, so the
    brief's "fails when reverted" is met for the configuration edit alone. *The walks*:
    the configuration edit walk's restated resume reads the move the last switch made and
    the time since it where no scan has run since, its round trip of a kept instance exact
    (the exemption for a give-back after the clock moved, "the known limit of §4.9's
    spike", retired, the check now stricter), and 20 configurations more, seed stream
    unchanged before them, drawn toward the trace (every version running `t1`, a candidate
    running it nowhere, the instances on the slow task, a test and an untest after three
    cycles, one cycle of 5 ms, a test and an untest at once), its reach
    `:round_trip_held` and `:resumed_after_hold`, which the parent's `plan.ex` fails; the
    lone edit walk's oracle restates the rule too. `{7613, 10, 19}` now passes, its round
    trip exact with no oracle relaxed.
  - *337, confirmed (b):* the suite's failure that named no test is left noted; the gate
    names a failed run's tests from ExUnit's manifest. Nothing built.
  - *338, confirmed (a):* a block's retained `var` stays hidden from `get/2`, as IEC hides
    a function block's internals and Logix an Add-On Instruction's local tags; its mark of
    provisional above dropped.

  IEC 61131-3 has no online edit, and says nothing of a timer whose instruction is not
  called for a while. Logix's test and untest of edits run the original's rungs or the
  edited ones, so a timer on a rung only one of them holds is not scanned while the
  other runs; whether a Logix TON or RTO not scanned for a while catches up the time
  when next scanned true is not checked here (unverified), as M6-8's question said.

  The README examples' harness, the mutants and the cost of the one plant's runs are in
  `scratchpad/m6/m9/`. 2412 tests (11 doctests), up from 2411. M6-9's review's fixes: 2415 tests (11
  doctests), up from 2412, the three provisional tests in `config_edit_test.exs`, and the
  done sentence's plant changed in place.

  **M6-9's answers** (the maintainer, 2026-10-31), decisions 339 to 342 in
  `docs/organisation.md` §7, built the same day. Questions 3, 4 and 5 were answered (b),
  each, and the one plant's "one write" confirmed (a). Together the three answers are one
  rule, which `Logex.Edit`'s moduledoc, `Logex.Configuration.Edit`'s, §4.9's Resume rows
  and `Logex.Edit.Plan`'s code state: **a timer's time runs only while a program that
  runs it holds the instance, and not while the instance is set aside.**

  *As built.* The edit's record of each instance (`Logex.Edit.Plan`) keeps `held`, the
  time from which the program that holds the instance has held it, and, new, `prior`,
  the time from which the other held it before, each nil from before the edit. A switch
  with no scan since this edit's last one and no time since it (`back?/3`: `switched` and
  the instance's own `now` still the switch's `at`; in a lone instance every switch with
  no scan since the last) only gives the instance back to the program that held it
  before: it gives back what the last switch moved (fix F11), resumes nothing more, and
  the two times swap, the program given it back holding it on from when it held it
  before. Any other switch ends
  the hold of the program it stops, scanned or not. A timer the program started runs and
  the program stopped does not, timing, resumes by `last + at - max(last, held)`, to `at`
  where `held` is nil, whoever scanned the instance last (`stopped_last?`, M2-5's "the
  program that last scanned", retired by decision 341). An instance back from aside
  (`Logex.Configuration.Edit`, whose edit gains `aside_at`, the time each instance it
  set aside was set aside) resumes each timer by `now - max(last, aside_at)`, none where
  that is 0 (decision 340). Decision 336's special cases, the resume from the switch only
  where no scan had run since and the give-back of a move after the clock had moved, are
  retired into the rule; its round trip after a hold still finishes on time.

  6. *Fix F11's undo after a cycle with no scan.* An instance whose timer the original does

     again: the test resumes the timer, three cycles pass with no scan of the instance on

     which runs the timer, held the instance those 30 ms. The operator sees nothing while
     the original runs, the timer frozen either way; at a later test the timer comes back
     with the candidate's 30 ms, where giving the resume back would give it the original's
     time instead. Options: (a) as built, the resume kept, exact by the rule; (b) give it
     back as fix F11 did across such cycles, the state exactly as the test found it but
     the next test's timer 10 ms off, the original's hold before the test counted; (c)
     left open. The reading taken is (a), provisional. *(Answered (a) by the maintainer,
     2026-11-01, decision 345.)*
  7. *A hold from before the edit.* A timer the original does not run, stopped by an
     earlier edit, which this edit's first test starts running again: the edit cannot know
     when the original began to hold the instance, so the resume takes all the time since
     the timer last ran, as decision 23 resumes it, though some of that time may have been
     held by an earlier candidate, which ran the timer. It needs no unusual sequence: an
     edit cancelled and accepted again is enough (M6-9's answers' review found it within
     one edit and one cancel). A fan's run-on `tof` whose rung the running program has
     lost, and a candidate that puts it back: tested, the candidate holds the fan's

     tested: the run-on loses those 18 ms, which the candidate, which runs it, held, and
     the fan runs on 18 ms longer than its delay. Nothing is taken from the original;
     time the first candidate held is lost. Options: (a) as built; (b) keep the time of
     every instance's last switch in the instance itself, so that a later edit knows it,
     the timer counting the earlier candidate's hold too, the fan on time; (c) left open.
