     `{:resumed, "c1.o1[1].lube", 50}`, the array built again once.
     `config_edit_test.exs`'s "one back from aside resumes each timer that was timing, in
     an array of timers or of blocks too, at every depth (decision 340)", over `@depths`
     and three more, a 2-D array of timers, a block's array of them and a 2-D array of
     such blocks, fails at the parent; `instance_array_test.exs`'s "bringing an instance
     back from aside allocates linearly in its array of timers" fails under a put into the
     tuple an element, 14.5x the words for 4x the elements, where the walk gives 4.1x.
     Decision 340's record, `Logex.Configuration.Edit`'s moduledoc and question 1 say so.
  2. *No edit step given `elapsed_ms` is exact.* The switch, `held` and `aside_at` read the
     resource's `now`, the last cycle's, not the step's own time, `now + elapsed_ms`, so
     the time between that cycle and the step goes to the program the step leaves holding
     the instance: a 10 ms task's lube tested 3 ms and untested 8 ms after a cycle comes
     back with the candidate's 5 ms counted, `acc` 20 where 15 is exact. Exactness would
     need a timer's `last` to stand past its instance's `now`, which decision 188
     refuses, or the step to move a clock. Not settled here: pinned as built, provisional,
     by `config_edit_test.exs`'s "a step given elapsed_ms switches at the resource's now
     (provisional)", and put to the maintainer, question 8 below; decision 339's reading
     (3) and both moduledocs say so.
  3. *Mutant N4, a hold's end forgetting `prior`, passed the full suite.* `edit_test.exs`'s
     "a give-back after two holds' ends counts the original's hold from its own untest,
     not from the timer's last run (decision 339)": a frozen lube, a hold's end at 30, a
     second at 40 and a give-back at once, then a test at 50 resumed by the original's 20
     ms since 30, where N4 resumes by 30. It fails under N4.
  4. *Mutant N12, the time set aside the step's own time, passed the full suite.* The test
     of finding 2 sets an instance aside with `elapsed_ms` 3 and brings it back with 4:
     resumed by the 50 ms aside by the resource's clock, where N12 gives 47. It fails
     under N12.
  5. *Question 7's example understated how ordinary its loss is.* An edit cancelled and
     accepted again loses the time the first candidate held unscanned. Question 7's
     example is now that sequence, the fan's run-on 18 ms long.
  6. *Pinned values changed beyond the answers' were listed only here.* Decision 339's
     record now lists them too: decision 56's follow-up `50 + 20 + 20`, decision 57's

  (`scratchpad/m6/a10/cost.exs`): an untest bringing back an instance of 1 bool and 1
  `rto`, 20 and 1, 100 and 1 and 20 and 10 took 932, 1,388, 4,589 and 1,996 at the
  parent, 948, 1,404, 4,604 and 2,021 at `e0d0a15`, and 903, 1,340, 4,480 and 1,623 now,
  the walk by type cheaper than the paths it replaces; a kept instance's switch is as at
  `e0d0a15`. The scan is unchanged.

  *Put to the maintainer*, numbered after M6-9's answers' two:
  8. *A step between two cycles.* `Logex.Runner` steps an edit between rounds and gives the
     time since its last round; the switch is taken at that round's time, so the time from
     the round to the step goes to whichever program the step leaves holding the instance.
     A box line's lube `rto` on a 100 ms task: tested 30 ms after a round and untested 80
     ms after it, before the next round, the lube counts the candidate's 50 ms and
     finishes 50 ms early; untested 70 ms after a round the candidate ran, it counts
     those 70 ms as the original's, early by as much. The error is at most the time since
     the last round, a task's interval at the most. Options, by what the operator sees:
     (a) as built, a timer early or late by up to the time since the last round across a
     step; (b) exact, the switch taken at the step's own time, which lets a timer's `last`
     stand ahead of its instance's `now` until the next cycle (decision 188 amended for a
     switch's own write) or gives the instance the step's time as its `now` (decision 56
     amended), the lube on time; (c) left open. The reading taken is (a), provisional.
     IEC 61131-3 has no online edit. Logix switches between the original's and the
     edited rungs as a program scan begins, so its switch is a scan's time too, the
     reading (a) takes; how a Logix timer counts the time between that scan and the
     operator's click is not checked here (unverified). *(Answered (a) by the maintainer,
     2026-11-01, decision 343.)*

  2424 tests (11 doctests), up from 2420: the seven-depth bring-back and the step given
  `elapsed_ms` in `config_edit_test.exs`, the give-back after two holds' ends in
  `edit_test.exs` and the bring-back's words in `instance_array_test.exs`.

**What stays deferred**, each a later item or milestone (§4.13): `persistent`, not
reserved (decision 280); `program retain` on a configuration's line (281); a retained
located global (272); a retained element of an array; an outage counted in wall time
(273); a program's first-scan bit, or knowledge of how it started (274); a pre-scan (279);
a hot restart; `VAR_CONFIG` and several resources in one store (Milestone 13); `constant`;
a warm restart that names paths to start cold (284); a store per program instance;
encryption or a checksum of the store beyond its grammar; retaining forces, which have
their own file; and the retention of the types later milestones add, Milestone 7's `TIME`
and Milestone 8's structures, which the store's header version lets change its format.

**Milestone 6 is done when** a box counter, a totaliser and a lubrication timer that a
program marks `retain` keep their values across a warm restart, across a runner killed
and started fresh from its store, losing at most what changed in one store period and one
write, and across a changed program, by name and type; a cold restart starts them at
their initial values, and a crash just after it brings none of the old values back; no
output comes back on from the store itself; and a program that marks nothing behaves
exactly as before.


### The review after Milestone 6 — 2026-11-01

The maintainer asked for a critical review of the whole codebase once Milestone 6 closed,
with a PMI and two pre-mortems, every finding tried and its refutation tried in turn. Four
workflows ran 27 reviewers at `d422608`, 63 agents in all: each reviewer attacked its scope
by running code (fuzzers, metamorphic tests, independent IEC oracles, random walks of the
edits and the runner, real-clock probes, mutation), a second agent in its own clone tried
to refute each finding, and a third tried to refute that verdict. Of 203 findings 13 were
refuted, each by a recorded decision, and 190 survive, 12 high, 35 medium and 143 low,
about 60 defects once merged. The report, with every finding, the PMI and both
pre-mortems, is `docs/review-2026-11-01.md`; its labels (H1 to H5, M1 to M17, and the
reviewers' own, `b5-config-edit-1`) are this section's and the report's alone.

What held: no reviewer found a wrong value from the evaluator (1,200 fuzzed programs, three
metamorphic relations over 1,300 more, IEC oracles of every timer and counter at every
width), the front end's round trip over about 100,000 mutated sources, the lone edit over
380,000 walk steps, and the runner's scheduling under 10,000 concurrent calls and a clock
jump of 10^9 ms. The defects gather where code reads again names the lexer has cut, at
combinations added late (a bit of a member of an element), in the runner's own work against
a real-time deadline, and in the configuration edit's held reasoning.

**The questions, answered by the maintainer on 2026-11-01**, decisions 347–360:

1. A held output an unwritten var_output is wired to (H1): kept held, decision 347.
2. One write's time limit (H2): each device its own, decision 348.
3. A retained `tof` held on at the outage (M3): it stays off, decision 349.
4. A trigger's sample whose task a trip cut off (M4): counted after, decision 350.
5. A rung that writes nothing (M5): refused, decision 351.
6. The runner's own long work (M7): cheaper and bounded, decision 352.
7. A stalled disk (M8): every write time-limited, decision 353.
8. A restart asked while running: judged when asked, decision 354.
9. A store cut short: an end line, `logex retain 2`, decision 355.
10. Two runners on one store: refused within one VM, decision 356.
11. Exact reduction pins: same-run bounds, decision 357.
12. CLAUDE.md: a slim index with a size test, decision 358.
13. The receipts and the toolchain: everything before Elixir 1.20 dropped, the checks
    committed, decision 359.
14. A store a fresh start drops from: a copy kept, `<store>.dropped`, decision 360.

**The items.** Each runs as every item does: built, reviewed adversarially, fixed, landed
and CI checked; each fix with a test that fails when it is reverted.

  index under a size test; the older-toolchain sandbox gone; README's examples checked by
  a test; the mutation and load scripts under `scripts/`; the report's stale and false
  claims made true (its "Documents and process" list, the stale comments of
  `runtime.ex`, the "provisional" marks decisions 343–345 settled, `Logex.IO.Point`'s and
  `Logex.Declarations`' moduledocs). *(Landed 2026-11-01, branch `rv1`: CLAUDE.md an index

- **RV-2 — the compiler** (decision 351). Every source text `Logex.compile/2` raises on
  given a diagnostic (H5's six roots, by one parsed-name structure the readers of a
  lexed name share, and M13's huge numbers); a one-shot's storage bit and a pulse bit in

  **RV-2 as built** (2026-11-01, branch `rv2`, five commits over `e365fa4`). Every finding
  below is closed with a test that fails when its fix is reverted (checked by reverting),
  or kept for the reason given.

  - *H5, the six roots* (`compile_total_test.exs`): a block rung led by an empty first leg
    at any depth (`element_line/1` passes an empty leg over); a literal bit number in
    brackets on an instance, told it has no bits as `t.[n]` is; a pulse bit in a bit of a
    member of an element, named `lc[1].pv.0` by `Logex.Walk.bit_name/1`; a bit number held
    in an array, told an array holds no one number; `cal` of a name that goes on past an
    element, its element lowered only where the name is one; and a lexed name that is no
    element. **The parsed-name structure**, `Logex.Name`: a name is its `.` parts, split
    once, exact since the lexer puts no `.` inside brackets, each part one of four shapes
    (a word, a word with one pair of brackets closing it, an integer, a bit number in
    brackets), read by the one reader of its shape: `element/1` (one word and one pair of
    brackets closing it, nothing else, where `Logex.Array.split/1` cut at the first `[`
    and took the text to the last `]`), `subscript/1` and `bracketed/1` (total), `base/1`
    (a type word's base, the loader's and the configuration reader's) and `word/1` (a
    host's key's array, however its brackets are written). Every former caller of
    `Logex.Array.split/1` and `subscript/1`, the compiler's bracket readers, the loader's
    `unsized`, the configuration reader's `base_word`, `Logex.IO`'s and `Logex.Declarations`'
    cuts read through it. The compiler's operand path still splits a name at `.` and tells
    each part's shape by its last byte in a clause's guard, as it did: a full walk of each
    name's bytes would have cost every operand of every program, and the per-part readers
    close the class, since the crashes came from a part reader given a whole name. Since
    RV-2's review `element/1` reads an element's name in one split, a reduction or two
    dearer than `Logex.Array.split/1`, where its first form cost 15 to 18 reductions to
    split/1's 4 and made a program of arrays up to 7.6% dearer to compile; a program
    compiles within 8 reductions a rung of what it did at `e365fa4`, one of arrays within
    16 (the most measured 13, a rung of three elements subscripted by tags, 0.7%), pinned
    in `compile_total_test.exs` ("the cost of RV-2's checks against the parent"), and every
    program scans in exactly the reductions it did.

    - a5-data-model-10's third (a column with no line not shown): a column alone names no
      place, and no stage gives one.
    - a6-compile-scale-8 (the 65,536-element limit counting each array alone, so an array
      of 256 blocks each holding `k[256]` of blocks holding `ton[256]` needs gigabytes):
      a limit on what an instance holds at every depth is a rule of its own, put to the
      maintainer below.
    - a6-compile-scale-9 (the loader recompiles a block shared by a chain of files once a
      file, d(d-1)/2 for a chain of depth d): decision 54's check, every type a compile is
      given recompiled from its source to be the one it says; trusting the loader's own
      types is a change to that decision, put to the maintainer below.
    - a6-compile-scale-14's link half (one directory reached through a link a second path):
      the memo is keyed by each path expanded, lexically; resolving links would read the
      file system for every path (provisional).
  - *Provisional readings*: the bounds, 10,000 characters and an exponent of 9,999; a rung
    of empty groups alone, which holds no line in the parse tree, cited at the first line
    it can stand on, after the rung before it, "a rung of empty groups alone, after line
    1"; a label alone refused as a rung that writes nothing; a link to a directory a path
    of its own in the loader's memo; since RV-2's review a rung the jump checks refuse
    told that it writes nothing too (question 7).
  - *Questions for the maintainer*, by what an operator sees *(all seven answered on
    2026-11-01, decisions 367 to 373: 2, 3 and 7 as built, 1, 4, 5 and 6 changed, to build
    in RV-9)*:
    1. *A jump to the end.* `jmp done` … `lbl done` on the routine's last rung is now
       refused, the label alone writing nothing (decision 351 read literally, and Logix's
       LBL needs an output after it). The operator writes `lbl done ote landed` with a tag
       of no use. (a) As built; (b) a label alone taken as a rung, the end of a jump, and
       refused only where nothing jumps to it; (c) a `nop` instruction for it, IEC having
       none, Logix's NOP.
    2. *A rung of empty groups alone*, `( )`, is cited at the first line it can stand on,
       so after blank lines its line is the one after the rung before it, not its own.
       (a) As built; (b) the parser keeps a group's line in its tree, which moves the
       front end's golden record, every group a line more.
    3. *A number's bound.* A literal past 10,000 characters, or a real whose exponent is
       past 9,999, is a lex error at its column; a store or forces file that holds one is
       refused at start. (a) As built; (b) a tighter bound, 100 characters, which no value
       of a type needs more than 25 of; (c) none, reading a long one slowly.
    4. *An instance's size at every depth.* `var row cell[256]`, a block holding
       `var c k[256]` of blocks holding `ton[256]`, compiles and needs gigabytes on its
       first scan. (a) As built, the limit an array's alone; (b) 65,536 elements counted
       through every array of instances an instance holds, refused at its line.
    5. *The loader's recompiles.* A chain of 30 blocks, each holding the next, compiles in
       435 recompiles, decision 54 checking every type given. (a) As built; (b) the loader
       trusting the types it compiled itself, so a chain costs its length.
    6. *Disjoint subscripts.* `ote ee[1,i]` and `ote ee[0,i]` are warned as two coils that
       may share an element, which they never do. (a) As built, the warning's "may"; (b) a
       subscript literal in the same place told apart, so rows that differ are no warning.
    7. *A misplaced label told twice.* `xic auto lbl done` is refused for its label, which
       stands first on its rung, and told too that the rung writes nothing, since moving
       the label first, `lbl done xic auto`, still leaves a rung that writes nothing.
       (a) As built, both; (b) the label's message alone, the second given once it is
       moved.

  **RV-2's review** (2026-11-01, of `cc98165`: eleven findings, each fixed with a test that

  1. *A connection's member that ends in `]` and is no element*, `k1.[0]` or `k1.o[1].[2]`,
     raised `FunctionClauseError` from `Logex.Configuration.compile/3`, `compile_file/1` and
     `check/1`, `Logex.Name.element/1` giving nil, which no clause took: it is told as a
     member its program does not declare, too deep where it has a `.` part, as `k1.a.3` is
     (`compile_total_test.exs`, H5's sixth root).
  2. *H5's first root not pinned*: a reading of a rung's line that stopped at a group's
     first leg survived the suite. A group alone whose first leg is empty, `( | xic a ote
     b )` or `( | ote b )`, compiles in a block and runs, and beside a rung of empty groups
     alone each is cited by its own line; a rung that writes nothing is cited by its parse
     tree's line, and a rung of empty groups alone by a walk of the tree once a routine
     holds one, so the citing no longer depends on how many markers there are.
  3. *A connection's instance with brackets*, `k1[1].a x`, raised the host's
     `ArgumentError` from `compile/3`: the configuration reader breaks the line, told the
     instance is named whole, and the line still connects `k1`'s `a`.
  4. *The compile's cost*: decision 351's check looks at a rung's last instruction first,
     and `Logex.Name.element/1` reads a name in one split (the H5 and decision 351
     paragraphs above); every program within 8 reductions a rung of `e365fa4`, one of
     arrays within 16, pinned.

     lowered, and a rung the jump checks refuse told both, pinned (question 7).
  6. *`Logex.Printer.print/1` of a routine whose rungs are no proper list* is the printer's
     pinned `ArgumentError`, where `Enum.map_join/3` raised.
  7. *An array of reals no rung writes* is told it stays at 0.0, as a real is.
  8. *`Logex.Declarations.a_or_an/2` of a word that is no binary* raises a pinned
     `ArgumentError`, where it raised `FunctionClauseError`.
  9. *The documents*: `docs/naming.md`'s `lbl` stanza amended, a label alone no longer a
     landing that does nothing; `Logex.Name.bracketed/1` made total, nil for a text of no
     bit number in brackets, so its comment's "each is total" is true.

  is false, keeps `.en` 1 and runs its delay at its first run with its rung false, a fan
  coming on for its run-on with nobody pressing anything; putting every retained `tof`
  with `.en` 1 and `.tt` 0 at rest at the restart and the start, which costs a scan
  nothing, or clearing every `tof` there as Logix's prescan does, its run-on among them,
  are the others. (13) A point a frozen var_output copies out, rewired by an edit to
  another frozen var_output that holds another value, moves at the first cycle with an
  empty forecast where it is a scalar, its old driver never having counted as one, and is
  held where it is an element of an array the old connection wired whole (decision 232's
  reading); holding both, or reporting the move, are the others. (14) A point no
  connection drove, newly wired from a frozen var_output, moves to the var_output's value
  at the first cycle with an empty forecast; holding it at its value, or reporting the
  move, are the others. (15) A var_output no rung writes but a rung reads, held at its
  point's value, changes what that rung gives, `xic aux ote lamp` turning the lamp off,
  reported only as `{:holds, "m1.aux", 0}`; holding no var_output a rung reads, the point
  moving instead, or refusing the edit, are the others. (16) An image's sample of a task
  the configuration started does not declare, which a store written at a cut round leaves
  when the configuration then drops the task, is refused at the start as a sample of no
  held global is; passing it by is the other.
- **RV-4 — the runner and its devices** (decisions 348, 350, 353, 354 and 356). Each
  device its own write limit (H2); every file write time-limited, a write's temporary
  file its own (M10); a restart judged when asked; one VM's runners on one path refused;
  `start: :cold` written after the name is checked (M11); an adapter's struct refused as
  no result (M6); an adapter whose first read fails closed (M14); `vetted/3` linear (M9);
  the report's runner and device lows.

  **RV-4 as built** (2026-11-01, branch `rv4`, eleven commits over `1bdc2c6` and a merge of
  RV-3's `d7a1290`). Every finding below is closed with a test that fails when its fix is
  reverted, each revert a mutant of `scripts/mutate.sh`'s tables judged by the full suite
  and red by the test named, or kept for the reason given. Decision 350, in this item's
  heading, is RV-3's and was not built here; nothing of `runtime.ex`, `instance.ex`, the
  edits, the configuration or `image.ex` was touched. RV-3's decision 350 runner tests,
  merged in, pass on RV-4's runner.

  - *H2, decision 348* (`trip_test.exs`): c3-io-contract-1 reproduced first, three runs of
    three on the real clock, a slow drive in time and a fast panel written after it, the
    panel killed in its own fast write and named. A round's write now gives each device
    the idle watchdog and a poll period from the start of its own write: where the clock
    has moved since the refresh before the writes, every device is refreshed again at the
    write's start, the device written hearing its own deadline and every other the runner
    well while it waits; a write in the millisecond of the last refresh needs none. On the
    manual clock a panel written after the drive's 509 ms write is in time where it takes
    5 ms more and is named for its own 510; on the real clock five devices, four slow in
    time (160 ms of 600 each, together past one shared deadline) and a fifth that hangs:
    nothing trips, then the fifth alone is named and every other takes the trip's 0. The
    comment of the test M4-6's sixth verification changed states the rule as it now is.
    Mutants: no renewal, and the deadline moved with no refresh, each red.
  - *Decision 353, M8* (c7-premortem-plant-2, b3-store-image-3, c2-runner-persist-4;
    `stalled_disk_test.exs`, new, not async): a force's write of the forces file and the
    store's writes at a trip, a stop, a shutdown, a cold restart and a fresh start are each
    made in a process of their own, `Logex.Runner.Writer.written/3`, waited on for the idle
    watchdog and a poll period of real time and killed past it: a force
    `{:error, {:forces, :timeout}}`, a store write `:timeout` reported as any failed write,
    the runner answering on. The forces file's read at a restart is limited the same and
    made raw, off the VM's file server, `{:error, {:forces, :timeout}}`, the runner tripped
    as it was (decision 390, which RV-11 changed: the restart carries on with the forces it
    holds). A stalled disk is acted out by the VM's file server held
    (`:sys.suspend/1`), which every write's rename goes through, and the restart's read by
    a FIFO in the forces file's place; a force, a trip's write, a cold restart's, a stop
    waiting on a period's write and on its own, a fresh start's and a restart's read each
    answer within four limits, the killed write's caller dead, and once the disk answers a
    write killed in its rename lands whole, the store the old or the new. Mutants: each
    limit `:infinity` in turn (the force's, the store's, the fresh start's, the restart's
    read) and the kill dropped, each red.

  - *Questions for the maintainer*, by what an operator sees *(the twelve open answered on
    2026-11-01, decisions 390 to 401: 4, 5, 7, 9 and 13 as built, 1, 2, 6, 8, 10, 11 and 12
    changed, to build in RV-11)*:
    1. *A restart on a stalled disk.* The plant trips, the disk stalls, the operator asks
       a warm restart: it answers `{:error, {:forces, :timeout}}` after 510 ms and the
       plant stays tripped, every output 0; and since RV-4's review a fresh start whose
       forces file the disk does not answer for 510 ms, or that is a FIFO, is refused, an
       `ArgumentError` saying the forces file cannot be read, nothing started. (a) As
       built; (b) the restart goes on with the forces the runner holds, the file unread,
       and says so, and the start with none, saying so.
    2. *A write that timed out.* A stop on a disk that stalls for a second answers
       `{:error, {:retain, :timeout}}`, yet once the disk wakes the store may hold that
       very write, since nothing can stop a call the kernel has begun; the operator who
       reads the message thinks the store is the old one. (a) As built, README saying a
       write that timed out may still land; (b) `status/1`'s `retain` saying the last
       write is unknown until a later one lands.
    3. *Withdrawn since RV-4's review.* A trip that came just after a restart was asked
       could be cleared by it, the restart judged as the runner took it from its mailbox;
       the review found that window as wide as a device's whole write limit, not a round.
       The trip now refuses every restart already in the mailbox, each asked while the
       runner ran, as decision 354 says, and nothing is left to choose.
    4. *One `.tmp` name.* Each write uses `tally.retain.tmp`, made new each time, where
       the review suggested a name a write; the operator sees at most one `.tmp` beside
       the store. (a) As built; (b) a name a write, `tally.retain.<n>.tmp`, the leftovers
       of writes killed on a stalled disk piling up beside the store until cleaned.
    5. *A card whose first read fails.* Its outputs are written 0 once before it is
       closed, as a device closed always is. (a) As built; (b) closed with no write,
       since no round ever wrote it.
    6. *A clock that goes wrong.* A host's clock that answers no whole number of
       milliseconds once the plant runs stops the runner, a shutdown naming the clock,
       every output 0 by the latches; the host starts it again. (a) As built; (b) a trip,
       the runner kept for a restart once the clock is mended.
    7. *A runner killed while a card hangs.* Its device is killed 510 ms after the
       runner, by the idle watchdog and a poll period, the card left as the hung adapter
       had it, since a killed device writes no 0, and free for the next start. (a) As
       built; (b) sooner, at the runner's death, the card left the same.
    8. *A busy HMI with no continuous task.* An HMI that calls `status/1` in a tight loop
       delays the 10 ms task, every request served ahead of a round due; the delay is an
       overlap the subscribers see. (a) As built, the share the continuous task's alone;
       (b) the share kept against the periodic tasks too where there is no untimed
       program.
    9. *A device's report backlog.* An adapter that reports thousands of changes in one
       poll period has them drained in time that grows with their square. (a) As built;
       (b) the device keeping a queue of its own, its messages then taken in another
       order, a change to what a restart reads first (decision 142).
    10. *A slow card's open.* An adapter whose connect takes 600 ms cannot start without
        an idle watchdog that loosens the plant's heartbeat too. (a) As built; (b) an
        `open:` limit of its own for the open and first read.
    11. *An address shown as text.* A trip for a misread address prints
        `{:unknown_address, ~c"\a"}`, the list `[7]` shown as a charlist. (a) As built;
        (b) a trip's address shown as its location's text, `panel.i.7`.
    12. *A busy machine's sync.* Every write's limit is the idle watchdog and a poll
        period, 510 ms unless set; on a machine whose cores are all busy a healthy disk's
        sync now and then takes longer, so a technician's force answers
        `{:error, {:forces, :timeout}}` and is not taken, or a stop answers
        `{:error, {:retain, :timeout}}`, though nothing is wrong with the disk. (a) As
        built, the host setting an idle watchdog that covers its disk; (b) a write's limit
        of its own, `write_limit:`, its default seconds, the heartbeat left as it is.
        RV-4's review met it again: decision 348's real-clock test, four writes of 160
        ms against 600, failed five runs of fifty under a load average of 10 to 13, where
        a sleep of 10 ms overshot by up to 668 ms; it is scaled since to writes of 600 ms
        against 2,100, and the long-write test to writes of 3,000 and 2,500 against 5,100.
    13. *A box counter's period write on a stalled disk* (RV-4's review). The SD card
        stalls; the period's write of the tally does not finish in 510 ms: the runner
        reports `{:retain, {:error, :timeout}}`, `status/1` says `failed: :timeout`, the
        writer is left to its write and the newest count waits for it, so the HMI shows one
        failure until the card answers, when the late write lands, the failure clears and
        the newest count is written next. (a) As built; (b) the late write killed as an
        event's is and the newest count handed at once to a new writer, the failure then
        reported again at every period while the card stalls, and each killed write's
        rename may still land when it answers.
  **RV-4's review** (2026-11-02, the review of `5208e60`; its probes under the review's
  scratchpad, `probes4/`). Eleven findings, each closed with a test that fails when its
  fix is reverted, each revert run by hand and the mutants rerun through
  `scripts/mutate.sh` judged by the full suite, or with a document made true:
  - *1, H2's real-time half* (`trip_test.exs`, "a write after a long one has the whole
    of its own limit"): the review's mutant, the wait taken from the deadline before the
    renewal, passed every test, since the manual clock's writes take no real time and the
    real-clock test's writes never outran what was left of a deadline. An idle watchdog
    of 5,000, a write of 3,000 ms and then one of 2,500: nothing trips, where the mutant
    cut the second at 2,100 ms, red.
  - *2, a killed runner's own write* (`stalled_disk_test.exs`): `Writer.within/2`'s
    process is linked to its runner, which traps exits, its exit taken with its answer and
    none left in the mailbox, so that a runner killed while it writes takes the write down
    with it, the write doing nothing after the call of the file system it was in; the
    review's repro, a killed runner's write renaming the next runner's `.tmp` into the
    store, is a write held in its delete on the held file server: the writer goes down
    with the runner, the store stays as it was and the next runner's cold write stands.
    Mutants: no link, red; the exit not taken, red by a trace of the runner's
    `handle_info/2`.
  - *3, decision 354 exactly* (`trip_test.exs`): every restart already in the runner's
    mailbox when it trips was asked while it ran and is refused there, decision 133's
    words, so a restart behind a device's change whose round trips (the review's
    manual-clock repro) and one asked while a round waits on a device's write (its
    real-clock repro, held here by an adapter that waits on the test) are each refused, and
    a restart asked after is served. The stamp taken as the runner takes a restart keeps
    the queue's; a restart in flight as the trip begins arrives after it and is the

  - *Decision 355, the end line* (b3-store-image-6, c7-premortem-plant-7;
    `retain_store_test.exs`, "a store cut short (decision 355)"): a store's first line is
    `logex retain 2` and its last its count of lines, `end <count> lines`, the header and
    the end line among them, as `wc -l` counts them (the words decision 409's):

    ```
    logex retain 2
    configuration plant written 2026-10-30T14:00:01Z
    global total dint 123557
    instance t1 counting
    t1.lamp bool 1
    t1.n dint 101
    t1.w real[3] 0.25 -2.5 3.4e38
    end 8 lines
    ```

    A store of version 2 whose last line is no end line, or whose end line counts other
    than its lines, is refused at a fresh start, `<store>: line <n>: ...`, the runner not
    started and no device opened; its last line is judged as the end line alone, so that a
    line a cut left half is told once, and an end line before the last is refused. Why a
    count of lines catches both kinds of cut: a cut keeps a file's first bytes, and the
    end line is the last of them; a cut at a line's end, or inside any line before the end
    line, a value's number cut in its digits among them (where version 1 read 1234567 cut
    to `12` as 12), takes the end line with it, and a cut inside the end line cuts its
    count, which is then smaller than the lines before it and it, which the cut did not
    change, or the word after it. Only a cut of the last newline alone keeps every line
    whole, and that store is read. The fuzz: a store a runner wrote cut at every byte
    offset, 181 cuts of its 181 bytes, each started on: 180 refused naming the file and a
    line, the last newline's read whole, every value the stop wrote; the store's reader
    alone pins the cuts at a line's end, inside a value's digits, inside a word and inside
    the end line's count and its word. The count also catches a line lost or doubled
    inside the file and a hand edit's added or removed line, the message saying so; any
    whole number the lexer reads is a count, `end 16#4 lines`, and none other, `four`,
    `-4`, `4.0`. A store of
    `logex retain 1` is read as before, a cut one among it (pinned: a cut at a line's end
    read short, a cut number read smaller), and a version past 2 is told this logex reads
    2 and 1. Every store written is of version 2 from now on. The test lines changed under
    the leave for a store's text: the encoded store's pin (header, `end 31 lines`); the
    unknown version's input made 3, version 2 being read now, and its message; the empty
    and foreign header's messages naming `logex retain 2`; `stalled_disk_test.exs`'s
    header pin; and the life walk's restated text, its header and its end line's count
    restated from the body. Mutants: no end line read, any count taken, the misplaced end
    line's clause dropped, any version read, no end line written, the cut line told twice,
    each red.

  - *Questions for the maintainer*, by what an operator sees *(all eleven answered on
    2026-11-02, decisions 409 to 419: 1, 3, 5, 7, 8 and 11 as built, 2, 4, 6, 9 and 10
    changed, built in RV-13 on 2026-11-04, each mark the decision's number)*:
    1. *A store's end line.* A store now ends `end 13 lines`; one cut short by a full disk
       or a lost tail is refused at start, naming the file and its last line, and the
       operator starts cold or restores a copy. A hand edit that adds or takes away a line
       must change the count. (a) As built, `end <count> lines`; (b) `end` alone, the count
       left out, catching every cut as well but no lost or doubled line inside the file;
       (c) a checksum line, catching a changed digit too, which a hand edit must then
       recompute.
    2. *A store's line ends.* A store an editor saved with CRLF line ends is refused at
       its first line, told the line ends with a carriage return and to save it with LF;
       a forces file saved so is refused as before, each line "no force", the carriage
       return invisible in the message. (a) As built; (b) both read as LF, as the source's
       and a configuration file's readers read them, which changes M5-11's pinned rule
       that a carriage return after a forces file's value is no force; (c) the forces file
       refused in the store's words too.
    3. *A store saved with a blank line at its end.* An editor that leaves an empty line
       after `end 13 lines` has the start refused, "an empty line, which a store never
       holds". (a) As built; (b) empty lines after the end line passed over.
    4. *The copy's name in status/1.* An HMI reads `status(runner).retain.copy`, present
       only where the start dropped something. (a) As built; (b) always present, nil where
       nothing was dropped, changing the map every start without drops shows.
    5. *A store that is a link.* An operator who keeps the store on a persistent card,
       `plant.retain -> /persist/plant.retain`, has the start refused and names the card's
       file itself. (a) As built; (b) the link followed, the store written beside the file
       it names, the link kept, two paths to one file then seen as one by decision 356;
       (c) as before RV-5, the link replaced by a file at the first write, the card's file
       left old.
    6. *A large plant's supervisor shutdown* (b3-store-image-4). A plant retaining 131,072
       timers takes some 5 s to make its store's text at a shutdown, past the child spec's
       5000 ms, and is killed in its write, the store keeping its last write. (a) As
       built, the host giving its own `shutdown:`, README saying so; (b) the child spec
       adding an allowance a retained value, counted from the configuration, a guess at the
       machine's speed; (c) left to RV-6's bound on the runner's own work.
    7. *A store's read at start.* A store on a stalled disk, or a FIFO in its place, now
       refuses a fresh start within the idle watchdog and a poll period, told the store
       cannot be read, as the forces file's read did until decision 390, which RV-11
       builds, has a start carry on with no forces. (a) As built, the start refused; (b)
       carry on as decision 390 has the forces file, from the configuration's initial
       values, saying so in `status/1`, the store on the stalled disk then written over by
       the first write that lands, every retained value lost unless decision 360's copy is

  *Questions for the maintainer*, continued, by what an operator sees *(answered on
  2026-11-02 with 1 to 7, decisions 416 to 419; 9 and 10 built in RV-13, 8 and 11 as
  built, each mark the decision's number)*:
  8. *A copy that cannot be made.* A changed configuration that drops a counter starts on
     a full disk, or with a directory where `plant.retain.dropped` goes: the copy fails,
     `status/1` shows `failed: :enospc` and `copy: nil`, and the plant runs; until the
     copy can be made no write replaces the store, so a crash or a stop meanwhile loses
     what changed since the start, the counts of boxes the line made since, and the next
     start drops the same counter again and tries the copy again. (a) As built, the start
     goes on, the store held until the copy is made, decision 275's rule for a failed
     write; (b) the start refused, as decision 291 refuses a cold start whose write fails,
     the line not starting until the disk is freed or the directory moved; (c) the start
     goes on and, after a number of failed tries, writes the store anyway, losing the
     drops. Logix has no such copy: a download replaces the project and its tags'
     values, and IEC 61131-3 leaves retention's medium to the implementer.
  9. *A cold start over a store refused as cut short.* A box counter's store is cut by a
     full disk; the start is refused naming its last line, and the message's remedy,
     `start: :cold`, writes a new store over it at once, its readable lines, the counts
     before the cut, gone unless the operator copies it aside first, which the message
     now says. (a) As built, the operator's to copy; (b) a cold start over a store it
     refused, or did not read, copies it first to `<store>.dropped`, as decision 360's
     copy; (c) a cold start refused while a store it cannot read stands, the operator
     moving it away first.
  10. *Rolling back a mistaken deploy.* A fan line's configuration is deployed with a
     counter retyped, the start copies the store to `plant.retain.dropped` and runs; the
     operator redeploys the good configuration without first putting the copy back: the
     good configuration drops the retyped counter from the store the mistaken deploy
     wrote, and copies that store over the copy, so the good counts, `t1.boxes.cv 50`,
     are gone. (a) As built, README telling the order, copy back first; (b) a copy a
     start, keeping each, `plant.retain.dropped.1`, `.2`, so none is replaced; (c) the
     copy kept while it is newer than the store, a start that drops replacing only an
     older one. Logix keeps no such copy; a download's values are the project's.
  11. *A long path in a refusal.* A store at a path of more than 4,096 bytes, which Linux
     does not open but a host's spelling through `..` can reach, is named in each line of
     a refusal as `…` and its last 4,096 bytes, and a line's 1,000 bytes are counted after
     the path. (a) As built; (b) the path cut shorter, 200 bytes, which changes the
     message for every path longer than that, many a test's directory among them; (c)
     whole, however long.

  - *Decision 456, a copy the same as the last skipped* (`af90bb6`, `fca47b3`;
    `retain_store_test.exs`'s "five starts that fail after their copy leave one copy", "a
    cold start refused after its copy, started again, makes no second copy" and "a FIFO
    at the highest copy's number is never read, the copy made past it"; the life walk's
    `same_copy/7`, `owed_numbered!/2` and its reach `:store_copy_same_kept`).
    `Logex.Runner.Writer.copy/3` reads the highest-numbered entry standing, raw and
    inside the copy's own limited process, where it is a regular file of the text's size,
    and where the bytes are the same makes no copy, `status/1`'s `copy` naming that one;
    a directory, a FIFO or an entry it cannot read is no match, the copy made past it;
    nothing is told before the copy is chosen to be made, so that a comparison cut off at
    the limit is a copy that failed, `:timeout` (decision 452). A fresh start that drops,
    a cold start over a store it would refuse and an owed copy made by a later write over
    one that landed late compare alike (provisional, the owed copy). The supervisor's
    loop of RV-13's question 8, the fan plant's, a deploy that drops and a device that
    cannot be opened, five starts, leaves `.dropped.1` alone where it left `.1` to `.5`.
  - *Decision 461, the devices let run first* (`af90bb6`; `trip_test.exs`'s "a runner
    that wakes late lets its devices run first", three tests on a clock that stalls the
    runner's next reading). A wake, a round's or a refresh's, later than its time by more
    than the idle watchdog while running sets the runner's `turn`, its time, and the look
    for a device not heard judges none within a poll period of it, each device's next
    poll; a device's word that it is back taken from then on is heard no earlier than the
    wake, its reply in the mailbox its turn though it read its clock before the machine
    stopped it; a hung device trips at the first look after its turn, every output 0.
    `status/1`'s `latest_wake` is every wake's lateness, a refresh's as a round's, where it
    was a round's alone (provisional). Each late wake gives a turn of its own, so that
    while every wake is late by more than the idle watchdog no device is judged
    (provisional). IEC 61131-3 leaves a controller's I/O faults to the implementer; Logix
    faults a module's connection only once it has missed four packets at its requested
    packet interval, never on one late look. The runner walk's hang was not given a
    late wake: a stall of the runner's reading at a wake moves its rounds past the
    schedule the walk's model keeps ("a round at 450, the schedule's at 44"), so the walk
    restates no 461 rule, the manual-clock tests holding it (a gap, question 3 below).
  - *The marks* (`fca47b3`). Each provisional mark of a reading decisions 448 to 454
    settle in `lib/logex/runner.ex`, `lib/logex/runner/` and the store's tests is the
    decision's number: 448, 449 (the stalled-disk test's name among them), 450, 452, 453
    and 454; the rest are RV-17's, outside the runner's files.

  *Provisional readings, put to the maintainer* *(answered on 2026-11-08 as restated
  after the review, below)*, by what an operator sees. The record is
  silent on each; the reading taken is the closest to it, IEC and Logix. IEC 61131-3
  leaves the runtime's faults and its I/O faults to the implementer; Logix names a major
  fault by its type and code and the task, faults a module's connection after four
  missed packets at its RPI, and keeps no copy of its retained memory.

  1. *A trip's name for the runner's own work* (decision 352). An HMI polls `status/1` of
     a box-counting line whose plant has grown to 40,000 instances of a block; one poll
     takes 600 ms, past `idle:`, and the line trips `{:watchdog, {:idle, 612, :status}}`,
     every output 0: the operator sees the HMI's own call named. (a) As built, the
     function the host called, an edit's step `{:edit, :test}`, `:period` for the
     period's hand-off; (b) the request whole, `{:get, "m1.count"}`, its arguments
     shown; (c) one name for every host request, `:request`, beside the edit's step and
     the period.
  2. *An owed copy compared too* (decision 456). A deploy drops the counter's value from
     the store, its copy cut off at the write limit on a slow card lands late as
     `.dropped.1`, and the next period's write owes the copy again: as built it finds
     `.dropped.1` holding the same bytes and makes none, `status/1` naming `.dropped.1`,
     where it made `.dropped.2`, the same bytes. (a) As built, every copy a start owes
     compared; (b) only a start's own copy compared, the owed one always written anew,
     two the same where one landed late.
  3. *A turn a late wake* (decision 461). A conveyor's host is so loaded that the runner
     wakes 600 ms late at every wake, and the drive's card hangs inside its read: as built
     each late wake gives the devices a turn of its own, so no device is judged until a
     wake comes on time, and the hung card trips the line only then, its outputs held
     meanwhile by the card itself. (a) As built; (b) one turn a lateness: a device silent
     through a whole turn trips at the next look, late or not; (c) a cap, a device
     unheard for four times the idle watchdog and a poll period tripping whatever the
     runner's lateness, as a Logix connection faults after four missed packets.
  4. *`latest_wake` every wake's* (decision 461). A fan's 1 s task has a refresh wake
     every poll; a 300 ms stall at a refresh now shows `latest_wake: 300`, where it showed
     0, only a round's wake counting. (a) As built, every wake's, the runner's own
     lateness the decision asks `status/1` to show; (b) `latest_wake` a round's alone and
     a key of its own for every wake, `latest_refresh`.
  5. *A device starved while the runner is inside a step* (decision 461, RV-7's question
     4). A lamp test's long step runs 200 ms, its panel starved by the host for 775 ms of
     it; the runner, not waking but back from its step, judges the panel at the next
     round and trips `{:io, "panel", :timeout}`, the panel healthy. Decision 461 gives a
     turn after a late wake; after RV-6 the heard-at-each-poll test failed so twice in 50
     under the busy loops, e1's step 975 and 820 ms, where its two failures in 50 at the
     parent were the late wake's, before any round, which no run at the tip met. (a) As built, a late wake alone gives
     a turn; (b) a step that runs past the idle watchdog gives the devices a turn before
     the next round's look, as a late wake does; (c) a device's silence over a step
     judged against the step's deadline, its task's watchdog and a poll period, which the
     devices were given before it.

  **RV-6's review** (2026-11-08, at `6a89a5e`; `scratchpad/rv/r6p/`): thirteen findings,
  the code's behaviour unchanged from the parent's under a differential fuzz of 600
  programs and 150 edits, 11 of 20 mutants surviving the full suite, two of them
  equivalent, and a real-clock test failing 11 runs in 50 under `scripts/load.sh` at the
  tip. Each became, at `9d5ad5a` and `a3b0e10` and this entry's commit:

  1. *The heard-at-each-poll test under load* (high). The new form, `Logex.IO.Sim waited
     5000 ms for … to handle its report`, was the device's, not the sim's: a device whose
     own poll read the change passed it on and waited on the runner with no poll armed,
     its next poll armed only once the runner answered, so it told the runner nothing
     while it waited, and e1's step waited 5 s for a word that never came; the panel's
     poll had read the set before the sim's report reached it, a race the parent has too,
     which RV-17's sim, whose read reads its device's mailbox first (decision 462), made
     likelier (a dump at the failure: the device in its wait from a poll's read,
     the runner's mailbox holding no word of it, the panel latched at 1010 ms). Fixed in
     `Logex.Runner.Device`: a poll arms its next once the adapter's read is back, before
     what it read is passed on, so that a device waiting on the runner for its own poll's
     change polls on and tells the runner at each poll, as one waiting for a report's
     does. `trip_test.exs`'s "a device waiting on the runner for the change its own poll
     read is heard at each poll meanwhile, on the real clock", a sim that reports
     nothing, so that every change is a poll's, red at `6a89a5e` every run (the panel
     never written, e1's step past its watchdog), its idle watchdog 1000 ms so that only
     that wait fails it on a loaded machine. Under `scripts/load.sh -n 50`, four busy loops,
     the heard-at-each-poll test alone failed none of 50 at `a3b0e10`, where the review
     met 11 at `6a89a5e`, and so did both with the sixteen other new and changed tests
     (`scratchpad/rv/p6/load_heard_fix.txt`, `load_fix.txt`); the twin at an idle
     watchdog of 50 failed 9 of its first 17 runs, a runner the machine stopped for 60 ms
     latching its panel by decision 125 or, its own step's word taken late, judging it,
     the first test failing none of those 17, and was given 1000 before it landed.
  2. *A late reading at a change-made round* (medium). Decision 461's lateness is now seen
     by the look for a device not heard itself, against the runner's wake still to come,
     whatever message brought the runner there (`Logex.Runner`'s `overdue/2`, called from
     `silent/1`), where only a wake measured its own: the review's probe, a 100 ms stall
     ended by the panel's change, now runs its round, the drive unjudged, and trips
     nothing; "a round a device's change makes before the runner's overdue wake lets the
     devices run first, as the wake would", red at `6a89a5e` with `{:io, "drive",
     :timeout}`. `latest_wake` is the most the runner found itself past its wake's time at
     a look (provisional, question 4 below). The look is made only while running, so the
     running guard on the turn went (the review's r07, equivalent).

  3. *Sustained lateness* (decision 461). A conveyor's host so loaded that the runner
     wakes 100 ms late at every wake, idle 50, and the drive's input card hangs inside its
     read: as built each late look gives the devices a turn of its own, so no device is
     judged until a wake comes on time, and in the review's probe the line ran some 6 s

     next look, late or not, which trips a healthy card the host keeps starving; (c) a cap,
     a device unheard for four times the idle watchdog and a poll period tripping whatever
     the runner's lateness, as a Logix connection faults after four missed packets at its
     RPI; (d) the turn given only for a lateness the runner's own work did not cause.
     IEC 61131-3 leaves I/O faults to the implementer.
  4. *The runner's lateness, seen at its look* (decision 461). A fan plant's host stops
     the runner for 100 ms, idle 50, and the panel's change reaches it before its overdue
     wake: since the review the round the change makes looks at the runner's wake still to
     come, finds it 90 ms late, gives the devices their turn and shows `latest_wake: 90`;
     before, that round judged at once and tripped the healthy drive, `latest_wake: 0`; and
     since RV-6 a refresh's wake counts as a round's. (a) As built, every look, a refresh's
     or a round's, whatever brought the runner to it; (b) a wake's own lateness alone, the
     change's round judging at once; (c) every look gives the turn, but `latest_wake` a
     round's wake's alone and a key of its own for the rest, `latest_refresh`.
  5. *A device starved while the runner is inside a step* (decision 461, RV-7's question
     4). The form the as-built load runs met, e1's step 975 and 820 ms and the panel judged
     at the next round's look, stands: a lamp test's step of 200 ms whose panel the host
     starves for most of it trips `{:io, "panel", :timeout}` though healthy. The review's
     11 in 50 were another cause, the device's own, fixed above; at `a3b0e10` under four
     busy loops the test failed none of 50, so the step form, met at a load average of 14
     to 27, was not met again here, and the question stands on the as-built's two. (a) As built, a
     late look alone gives a turn; (b) a step that runs past the idle watchdog gives the
     devices a turn before the next round's look; (c) a device's silence over a step
     judged against the step's deadline, its task's watchdog and a poll period.
  6. *A copy spelled otherwise* (decision 456). A box-counting line's store has a copy a
     technician restored by hand as `tally.retain.dropped.007` beside logex's
     `tally.retain.dropped.6`, the same bytes the store holds; a deploy drops a counter.
     As built the comparison reads `tally.retain.dropped.7`, logex's own name, finds
     nothing, and makes `tally.retain.dropped.8`, `status/1` naming it, the same bytes as
     `.007`. (a) As built, the copy at logex's own name compared alone; (b) every entry at
     the highest number compared, a match on `.007` making no copy, `status/1` naming
     `.007`, a name logex never writes; (c) an entry spelled otherwise not counted for the
     number either, the copy made at `.dropped.7` beside it. Logix keeps no copy.
  7. *What the period's hand-off copies* (decisions 352 and 455). A fan plant's program
     of 65,536 rungs retains one bool; each period the runner sends its writer the whole
     resource, 36 ms of its own work, 91 ms for ten instances, where taking the one bool
     out cost nothing. (a) As built, the whole resource, the cost following the plant's
     size; (b) the programs' code left out of what is sent, about half for that plant;
     (c) the retained values picked out in the runner and sent alone, their text made in
     the writer, the cost following what is retained. IEC 61131-3 leaves retained data's
     storage to the implementer; Logix writes no store.

  **RV-7 as built** (2026-11-04, branch `rv7` over `0b026e5`). Decision 357 for every pin of
  the census above, each bound against a twin measured in the same run, in the same VM, each
  count in a process of its own whose heap no collection visits; and the load failures, each
  run under `scripts/load.sh` and root-caused, four fixed in the tests' measurement, two in
  their synchronisation, two shown closed by RV-11's decisions 398 and 400, and the rest the
  machine's starving the VM, none a fault of the runner's code. The rule and how to write a
  new one are `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s "Hold a cost against a twin measured in the same run" and
  "A count moves with the VM's own state"; what a runner test's count holds besides a round,
  and the orders a real-clock test may not assume, are added to its "A cost a scheduler's
  interleaving moves" and "Wait for a process's `DOWN`". No test, walk or oracle was deleted;
  as built here two were weakened, which RV-7's review found and mended (below): the step of
  `trip_test.exs`'s heard-at-each-poll test, which waited for one `back` and so passed a
  device that told the runner at one poll in 30, and the margins of half the guarded work,
  which passed every regression under that half and some the old pins caught. Each pin's
  line became a bound in the same test, and
  `retain_test.exs:1127`'s, `retain_edit_test.exs:515`'s and
  `retain_configuration_test.exs:1327`'s equalities bounds in the guarded direction,
  decision 357's leave. The load failures' changes replace a measurement or add a
  synchronisation, the lines they remove `retain_period_test.exs`'s two least-of-nine reads,
  `retain_image_test.exs`'s single counts and `trip_test.exs`'s bare monitors, each read
  again as the load failures below say, every assertion as it was.

    where it has no feature (M5-10's reals, decision 222's arrays, M5-13's located
    arrays, M6-2's blocks that retain nothing): the same program beside the feature,

  - *The load failures* (each run under `scripts/load.sh`, four busy loops on four cores,
    at the tip, the runner's code traced in a copy where a trace is said, never landed;
    the machine also ran this item's mutation table and another workflow's suites, a
    load average of 12 to 35 and the kernel's CPU pressure at 89 to 91%, harder than the
    busy loops alone):
    - `trip_test.exs`'s "a device waiting on the runner for its change is heard at each poll
      meanwhile, on the real clock, short" (idle 50 ms). Three causes, each traced. (a) The
      panel did not run during e1's 200 ms step: one `back` 9 ms in and none until the
      runner's next round at 286 ms, so it was found silent (run 24 of 50 at `ff7be44`);
      traced closer in a later run, the panel polled 10.5 and 15.2 ms in and then nothing,
      the runner's sleep ended at 216.6 ms and found the panel silent at 216.7, both timers
      coming due when the VM's scheduler came back and the runner running first, which no
      rule of the runner's is about. Fixed in the test's synchronisation: the step,
      `Sleeps`, sleeps its 200 ms and then lasts until the panel has told the runner, within
      its last poll period, that it is back, read from the runner's mailbox and left there,
      a 5 s cap ending the wait for a panel that tells nothing; red on a device whose
      waiting poll tells nothing and on a runner that judges silence before taking its
      notices (t2 and t3 below), and met in none of the fix's 100 runs, where the old form
      met it in one of 50 and one of the traced 30. (b) The panel not scheduled for 60 ms at
      another moment, before any round: no `back` since the runner's start for 99 to 156 ms,
      the runner itself idle 50 to 136 ms between two lines of `rounded/1` (six of 30 of a
      traced run at a load of 35, and one in each 50 of the new forms below, `rounds: 0`).
      (c) The runner not scheduled: e1's 200 ms sleep took 1120 ms, past its task watchdog
      of 1000 (run 11 of 50 at `ff7be44`; twice in the traced 30, 1060 and 1164 ms, and once
      in the new forms' first 50, 1363). (b) and (c) are the machine's starving the VM past

  **RV-7's review** (2026-11-04, of `2233434`; the review's evidence under
  `scratchpad/rv/review7work/`, this round's under `scratchpad/rv/rv7work/`, its mutants
  `mut2/`). Each finding and what it became:

  1. *The heard-at-each-poll test weakened* (high). Its step waited for one `back` from the
     panel, so a device that told the runner at one poll in 30 (t5) passed it, 5 of 5,
     where the old form tripped. The step now also counts what the rule is about: the
     polls the panel ran during the step, each armed on its clock, `Counted`, a test clock
     that is the machine's in every callback and counts each `{Logex.Runner.Device, :poll,
     _}` it arms, against the `back`s the panel sent the runner meanwhile, which stay in the
     runner's mailbox while the step runs: a poll tells the runner and then arms the next,
     so the polls are at most the `back`s and one, the poll running as the step began,
     however few the machine let the panel run. 17 to 20 of each in a step here; t5 red,
     "the panel ran 30 polls in e1's step and told the runner 1 times", t2 red, three of
     three each; under `scripts/load.sh -n 50`, 2 of 50 failed, each a trip `{:io, "panel",
     :timeout}` after e1's step ran long, 488 and 662 ms, the panel not scheduled for 288
     and 462 ms of its wait, and then not heard again within the idle watchdog after it:
     cause (b) above, the machine's, question 4 (decision 461). The count's assertion
     passed in every run that reached it.
  2. *The converted bounds missed regressions the old pins caught* (high). Every bound is
     now the twin's figure and what the two measured apart, the guarded path's own cost,
     with an allowance under the least regression the bound is for, half a reduction a
     unit or one a group, never half the guarded work; and where every program takes the
     guarded clause, the twin is one that takes another clause making the same calls:
     `real_test.exs` an `add` against a `div` (m03 red, 38 against 35 - 1 + 0.5) and a `gt`
     and its coil against a contact and a `move` (m03g, a comparison that looks the reals
     up, red); `tag_bit_test.exs` and `tag_subscript_test.exs` each two-instruction rung
     de-energised, a latch, a `move`, an `add`, a `not` and a `shl`, against a latch on a
     caught operand, 21 against 22, and an `add` pair (m01 and m09 red); `array_test.exs` a
     key's cost held 23 under the twin's, `+ 0.5` (m04 red, 39.0 against 38.47), and an int
     element's check against the test's own guarded walk over a tuple of its size, one
     reduction an element each, `+ 0.5` (a18b, an int element a call dearer, red, 2.0
     against 1.5); `located_array_test.exs` the cycle `- 22 + 1` a group (m05 red, 113.9
     against 106.7), the copy-out also against the same configuration's outputs located,
     whose copy-out reads its array and maps no plain point, `- 2 + 0.5` a point (m10 red,
     6.59 against 5.09), and the restart `- 5 + 1`; `retain_test.exs` the walk held, 12 and
     14, `+ 0.5` (r1b, an unmarked instance's guard a call dearer, red, 20 against 19.5);
     `bit_string_test.exs` each look's difference less half a reduction a rung (m07 red),
     contacts and a coil on bools against the same on a word's bits, 413 a rung apart (a
     name split twice red, 33 a rung), and an `add` against a `shl`, 68.9 apart (one
     class's operands grouped red, 44 a rung, which no form caught before); `real_test.exs`'s
     warnings less half a reduction (k5b, the guard's clause a call dearer, red).
  3. *Exact pins left in place* (medium). The six bounds at their limit, listed above
     under "Left as they are", have decision 357's half a reduction; m04, which touches
     only put_inputs/3, no longer turns `bit_string_test.exs:2007` red.
  4. *A probe on a call both twins make* (medium). `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s recipe said a call
     both twins make; it now says a call both make as often. The bounds whose twins read
     unequally hold that read's cost as part of the guarded path, and say so: a tag's bit
     reads its number (`tag_bit_test.exs:906`), an element's bit its element and a tag's
     bit takes its word through `Map.get/3` (`element_bit_test.exs:459`), a member through a
     tag subscript its subscript and an element's run its element, written back
     (`instance_array_test.exs:2507`), and a shift its count (`bit_string_test.exs:2007`);
     `long_timer_test.exs:1029`'s two runs read as often, and its red under the review's
     probe was its hundredths at the limit (19.0 under each read one, three and five
     dearer, with the half). Under the review's
     probes those are the tests red, and only those, judged by the full suite (the table
     below): `p_read_1`, `_3` and `_5` and the review's m02, every read caught, red on
     `tag_bit_test.exs:906`, `element_bit_test.exs:459`, `instance_array_test.exs:2507` and
     `bit_string_test.exs:2007`, `p_write_3` on the element's two; `element_bit_test.exs`'s
     `element <= tag + 0.5`, RV-7's form of the pin `element == tag`, is one of them, its
     twins a read apart as the pin's were, and every twin chosen in this review passes
     them.
  5. *The warm restart against a cold one, under load* (medium). One VM's restart count is
     the same from call to call while the VM's state holds (450 pairs, 16248 each here) and
     moves by a few reductions when it changes; beside a full suite the state moved within
     the test's eighteen counts, so each least of nine came from a state of its own. Now
     the pair counted nine times one after the other and the least of the differences
     held (`paired/2`), the difference within one state, which a regression moves in every
     pair (w1 red, 627 against 556 + 4); the same for `retain_test.exs`'s first scan and

  *Provisional readings, and questions for the maintainer* *(all seven answered on
  2026-11-07, decisions 458 to 464: 1, 3 and 6 as built; 2, 5 and 7 changed, to build in
  RV-17; 4 changed, to build in RV-6)*:

  1. *A twin that does the guarded work itself gives a lower bound* (decision 458, as
     built). Where a program of none takes a `nil` clause, its twin is the same program
     beside the feature, which does the feature's work: `put_inputs/3` over 64 inputs
     costs 37.875 reductions a key with no array and 60.97 beside one. As RV-7 first built
     it the bound was half that work apart, `none <= beside - 11`, which passed a program
     of none that walked its keys, 39 a key (RV-7's review); since then it holds the whole
     difference, 23, and half a reduction a key, `none <= beside - 23 + 0.5`, which
     catches a call a key. Made cheaper, the feature's own work now turns the bound red
     with no regression: an array's key check brought down by 2 a key puts the bound at
     36.47, and a program of none, still 37.875, fails it by 1.4. (a) As built: the
     difference held, so a maintainer who makes a feature cheaper sees its bound go red in
     the same commit and restates it there, said so beside each such test; (b) half the
     work as the margin, as RV-7 first built it, which a maintainer never needs to restate
     and which passes every regression of a program of none under half the feature's work;
     (c) a seam in `lib/` that runs the same program with the guarded clause skipped, a
     twin differing only there, which no module has, `lib/` being RV-16's and RV-6's now.
  2. *A regression that makes both twins dearer is caught by no twin* (decision 459, (b),
     RV-17). By the rule's own
     probe a call both twins make as often, dearer, leaves the bound green: so is a
     regression there. RV-7's review's survivors are each caught now by a twin that takes
     another clause making the same calls (M5-8's "a name split twice" and "one class's
     operands grouped" among them, which no form caught before); what no twin can see is
     a change to what every twin of a bound shares, each instruction's dispatch, each read
     where both read as often, each instruction lowered, which is what the probes charge.
     A read made a call dearer everywhere, for one, is red only on the bounds whose twins
     read unequally (finding 4) and in the growth tests' ratios not at all. (a) As built,
     such a regression left to those bounds and to review; (b) one ceiling a stage kept
     against a recorded figure, with a margin no toolchain's reduction reaches, twice the
     figure, which catches a doubling and not a call; (c) a count of logex's own calls in
     each scan a pin measures, by `:erlang.trace_pattern/3` with `call_count` in a module
     of its own run `async: false`, which a toolchain's code generation does not move and
     a call added anywhere does, held to the count measured at a commit.
  3. *Half a reduction a rung* (decision 460, as built). A scan's pair is allowed half a
     reduction a rung over what the two measured apart, since a rung's count moves by
     hundredths as the larger program's maps grow (58.02 against 58.0 in one pair); a
     regression of less than half a reduction a rung passes. (a) As built; (b) the pairs
     over larger programs, which only moves the hundredths further; (c) no allowance, red
     on the hundredths.
  4. *A device the machine did not schedule is a hung one* (for RV-16; decision 461, (b),
     RV-6). By decision 114 a
     device unheard for the idle watchdog and a poll period is hung, whatever kept it
     from running: under this item's load (a load average of 25 to 35 on four cores)
     `trip_test.exs`'s idle of 50 ms found the panel silent before any round, its process
     not scheduled for 99 to 156 ms, the runner idle for 50 to 136 ms between two lines of
     its own. When the VM's scheduler comes back, the runner's wake and the device's
     overdue poll come due together, and the runner, run first, judges the device before
     it has polled: in one traced run the panel polled 10.5 and 15.2 ms into the runner's
     200 ms step and then nothing, the runner's sleep ended at 216.6 ms, 16 ms late, and
     it found the panel silent at 216.7, the panel's overdue poll not yet run. A plant on
     an overloaded host would trip `{:io, "panel", :timeout}` with its panel well. (a) As
     built, the idle watchdog sized by the operator for the host; (b) the runner, back
     from a wake late by more than a poll period, lets its devices run before it judges
     them, or renews their heard times as decision 348 does while it waits on its disk;
     (c) a device judged silent only at two checks a poll period apart. RV-7's review's
     runs met it again, in the heard-at-each-poll test's new form 2 of 50 under the busy
     loops, each after a step whose wait for the panel ran 288 and 462 ms, and in
     `end_to_end_test.exs`'s real-clock plant at its default idle watchdog of 500 ms, once
     a trip and once fewer than 20 rounds in 2 s.
  5. *The real-clock reread test cannot hold the one read it needs* (decision 462, (b),
     RV-17). `trip_test.exs`'s
     "on the real clock, a bad reading of a device released while the one before it is
     read again trips nothing" needs a panel poll within the 700 ms the drive's reread
     sleeps; under load none came and the panel's own reread met the bad value (one in 50
     in RV-11's review, three in 100 here). A sim held, `:sys.suspend/1` or a `{:delay,
     ms}` of its own, holds whichever of the drive's reads comes first, a tripped device
     polling too, so the test cannot say its reread is the one held, nor wait for the
     panel's release without missing it. (a) As built, a real-clock twin of the
     manual-clock tests, exposed to the machine; (b) `Logex.IO.Sim` given a hold of the
     device's next reread alone, released by the test, a seam in `lib/` (RV-16's or
     RV-13's to give); (c) a tripped device that reads nothing at its polls, writing only
     its 0 again (decision 262), so that a sim's next read after a trip is its reread, a
     rule of the device's.
  6. *An edit's bound no mutant parts* (decision 463, as built). `retain_edit_test.exs`'s
     "an edit of programs that retain nothing pays nothing for `non_retain`", `==` before
     and `marked <= unmarked` since, met no mutant that moves one side and not the other;
     kept, read as a statement of the rule more than a guard, as M6-6's review read its
     `status: :running`.
  7. *A load waits on every other file call of the VM* (RV-7's review; decision 464, (b),
     RV-17). `Logex.SourceFile` stats and reads a program's files through the VM's file
     server, `File.stat/2` and `File.read/1`, which serves every file call of the VM one
     at a time; a sampler of its queue through a loaded suite found 2 to 9 calls waiting
     and none holding it, and two tests of thousands of loads, `configuration_test.exs`'s
     loader over 250 program types and `review_lows_test.exs`'s 300 loads beside a
     swapper, ran past ExUnit's 60 s where alone under the busy loops they take 0.5 s and
     2 s. A host that compiles a plant's files in a VM that also writes many files, a
     logger or a store, waits behind each of those writes for each file its plant names.
     (a) As built: the swapper's writes made raw, the loader's calls through the server,
     so those two tests stay exposed on a machine as loaded as the review's; (b)
     `Logex.SourceFile` stats and reads raw, `[:raw]`, as the runner's store and forces
     reads do since decision 390, so that a load waits on no other process's file calls, a
     change to `lib/` (RV-16's or RV-6's); (c) the tests of many loads in a module of
     their own, `async: false`, run when no other test's calls share the server, which
     leaves a host's load as it is.

  1. *An edit's accept over a large array* (a4-warnings-walk-5). A sorter with `var lane_t

    the label, which does nothing, so a jump to the end over a skipped rung holds its coil

  *Readings put to the maintainer, each now its decision's* *(all eight answered on
  2026-11-01, decisions 402 to 408, 2 and 7 as one: 1, 5, 6 and 8 as built, decisions
  402, 406, 407 and 408, and 2 and 7, 3 and 4 changed, decisions 403, 404 and 405, built
  in RV-12 on 2026-11-02)*. The record is silent on each; IEC and Logix say nothing that settles
  them.

  1. *A label alone a jump names, used twice* (decision 367). `xic a jmp done`, `lbl done`,
     `lbl done`: the second label alone is told only that `done` already labels the rung
     above, since a `jmp` names its label. (a) As built; (b) only the rung a jump lands on,
     the first, is a landing, so the second is told too that it writes nothing.
  2. *What a declaration counts at every depth* (decision 370). A block holding two
     `int[40000]` compiles, but `var x two` in a program is refused, 80,000 elements; and
     an element of an array of blocks counts its block's elements, so `cell[256]` of a
     block holding `ton[256]` is 65,536, taken. (a) As built, a declaration's leaf
     elements summed; (b) each array alone, multiplied through the arrays of instances
     that hold it, so `var x two` is taken and only nesting is bounded; (c) every element
     at every level, so `cell[256]` of `ton[256]` is 65,792, refused. A configuration's
     program instance is counted by none: each of its program's declarations is.
  3. *The loader's trust* (decision 371). The trust is an internal function the loader
     calls, `Logex.Compiler.loaded/2`; a host that calls it itself, outside the host
     contract, hands in a type unchecked. (a) As built; (b) a check that the types are
     the loader's own, by a token only the loader's call holds. The loader still reads a
     block's file once for each file that names it, to tell a block from a program: a
     configuration of 20 programs over one chain reads `b1.ld` 21 times, linear; reading
     it once a call is the other. Since RV-9's review `loaded/2` holds what it is handed
     to a type list's shape, junk refused in the words a compile's `types:` is; a type
     forged inside, an extra member or junk in its members or rungs, is trusted, and may
     compile or raise what the compile meets, which (b) would close too.
  4. *What decision 372 tells apart* (decision 372). `ote w[i].3` beside `ote w[j].4`,
     two bits of one word array through tags, is still the "may share" warning, a bit's
     number being no subscript; and a write through a tag subscript beside a one-shot's
     storage bit, `ons e[1,1]` and `ote e[i,0]`, which can never meet, is still warned as
     a write of the storage bit. (a) As built; (b) the bit's number as one more place;
     (c) the storage-bit warning judged as decision 372 judges two writes.
  5. *The fragment's setup* (decision 365). The test writes its own setup, `packing.logex`
     on the manual clock with the panel's first write slowed 2 ms, rather than cutting
     README's `on_the_clock.exs`, and holds the count of advances to 1 to 4, where this
     setup makes it 1. (a) As built; (b) README's own setup with the slow write added,
     and the exact count.
  6. *`wired.logex`'s first line* (decision 363). README shows it with no comment line,
     so the connection stays on line 7 and the warning README prints is unchanged. (a) As
     built; (b) a comment line as `tally.logex` has, the warning citing line 8.
  7. *An instance that is no array's element* (decision 370; RV-9's review). Decision 370
     counts through arrays, so an instance outside one counts nothing of its own: a block
     of 200 single `ton`s holds 0, and `var x wide[65536]`, 13,107,200 timers, is taken;
     a chain of blocks each holding two single instances of the one below, `d1` a `ton`,

  force, ran together under `scripts/load.sh -n 50`, four busy loops on four cores beside
  other suites: 0 of 50 runs failed. Each commit's gate printed GATE-OK, 2,710 at the tip
  (2,699 tests and 11 doctests), 23 more than the parent's 2,687; one gate before
  `a59715d` failed on `retain_configuration_test.exs`'s warm-against-cold cost, 6
  reductions over under the gate's load, which that commit reads as the least of nine runs
  where it read three (16,246 both, quiet). `5c80545`, which changed two test files only,

  store and a long period costs within a few reductions of none" read 11.7 against 10,

  runner call's timeout, `{:retain, :timeout}`, `{:forces, :timeout}` and `{:io_init,
